Antes de me converter, nunca tinha ouvido o termo “anabatista”, e a ideia de alguém compartilhar sua fé em Jesus com outras pessoas me era estranha. Depois de me converter, lembro-me de pensar em todos os meus amigos que não sabiam nada sobre o que acabara de acontecer comigo. Uma coisa não saía da minha cabeça: “Preciso contar a eles!” Quando algo bom acontece a alguém, essa pessoa geralmente conta aos outros. Algumas pessoas contam a uma ou duas pessoas, enquanto outras sentem vontade de contar a todos. Era isso que eu queria fazer, não por mim, mas por eles.

Sempre que encontrava um velho amigo, contava-lhe o que havia acontecido comigo. Geralmente, diziam que já tinham ouvido falar disso e depois tentavam me fazer ficar tranquilo e relaxar. Admito que cometi erros naqueles primeiros anos. Percebi que muitas pessoas não apreciavam o que eu tinha a dizer, mas o que mais me espantou foi que as pessoas que se diziam cristãs pareciam ser as mais ofendidas.

Um dia, eu conversava com um homem mais velho que disse ser cristão havia quase toda a vida. Durante a conversa, ele apontou para uma lâmpada e disse: “Está vendo aquela lâmpada? Ela não fala.” Fiquei chocado. Ele estava me dizendo que, sim, Jesus diz que somos a luz do mundo, mas que as luzes são silenciosas. Elas não falam. Fui para casa fazer um estudo bíblico pessoal sobre o assunto. Será que isso era verdade? Não demorou para eu encontrar versículos como: E Jesus percorria toda a Galileia, ensinando nas sinagogas deles, pregando o evangelho do reino e curando toda sorte de doenças e enfermidades entre o povo. –Mt 4:23. Além disso, em Mateus, Jesus diz que teve compaixão porque as pessoas que estavam com ele estavam cansadas e dispersas. Mais adiante, lemos: Então disse aos seus discípulos: A seara é realmente grande, mas poucos são os trabalhadores. Rogai, pois, ao Senhor da seara que envie trabalhadores para a sua seara. –Mt 9:37-38

Parece-me que, aonde quer que Jesus fosse, ele falava às pessoas sobre o reino. Já vi pessoas testemunhando sobre Deus de uma maneira desagradável. Isso não significa que não devemos testemunhar. Se você ler o livro de Atos, é praticamente só isso que verá: crentes compartilhando a mensagem do Evangelho com outras pessoas! Em um relato, as autoridades prenderam os discípulos e disseram que poderiam ser libertados se ficassem calados! Os discípulos, porém, disseram que não podiam: Porque não podemos deixar de falar das coisas que vimos e ouvimos. –At 4:20. Por fim, foram silenciados para sempre — pela morte.

Mais tarde, ouvi falar dessas pessoas chamadas anabatistas. Comecei a ler sobre elas e sobre como também não se calariam. Encomendei o Martyrs Mirror e fiquei espantado com o que li. Essas queridas pessoas viviam como os discípulos que encontramos na Bíblia. Cumpriram o que Jesus disse: E sereis odiados por todos por causa do meu nome; mas aquele que perseverar até o fim será salvo. –Mt 10:22. E, em Romanos: Como está escrito: Por tua causa somos mortos o dia todo; somos considerados como ovelhas para o matadouro. –Rm 8:36. Depois de algum tempo, encontrei uma igreja com uma visão anabatista.

Então, por que estou escrevendo isto? Queridos irmãos e irmãs, creio que o fogo está se apagando. Continuo ouvindo algumas pessoas entre os nossos anabatistas falarem sobre viver uma vida tranquila e pacífica. Jesus nos diz na parábola do semeador: O que foi semeado entre os espinhos é aquele que ouve a palavra, mas os cuidados deste mundo e a sedução das riquezas sufocam a palavra, e ela se torna infrutífera. –Mt 13:22. Será que alguns de nós estão nessa situação? Vivemos numa cultura ocidental em que parece fácil obter dinheiro, e nos concentramos em nossa própria riqueza e nos cuidados deste mundo. Tenhamos cuidado para não nos tornarmos como o mundo, a fim de evitar sermos perseguidos pelo mundo.

Um grupo de anabatistas fugia da perseguição e mudou-se para um país onde ainda não eram perseguidos. Começaram uma loja de móveis para se sustentar, mas não conseguiam vender nenhum móvel porque eram os temidos anabatistas. Logo a situação ficou desesperadora, pois precisavam de dinheiro para comprar comida. Um dia, um homem rico entrou na loja. Todos os trabalhadores pararam de trabalhar. “Talvez este homem compre alguma coisa, e possamos comer!”, pensaram. Um irmão idoso se aproximou do possível cliente e perguntou se ele conhecia Jesus. Depois de uma breve conversa, o homem saiu da loja furioso. Logo, alguns trabalhadores famintos perguntaram ao idoso por que ele precisava afugentar a única chance que tinham de fazer uma venda. Ele explicou que era muito mais importante aquele homem conhecer Jesus do que eles se preocuparem em fazer uma venda. Essa era a mentalidade dos primeiros anabatistas: o Evangelho vinha em primeiro lugar. Eles não podiam deixar de falar das coisas que tinham visto e ouvido e também eram mortos o dia todo.

Li numerosos relatos de cristãos anabatistas dos primeiros tempos que haviam sido presos por causa da fé. As autoridades imploravam que simplesmente ficassem calados! Mas eles se recusavam, assim como os discípulos. Também escolheram a morte, em vez de uma vida tranquila. Um jovem foi preso e deixou para trás sua querida esposa, que esperava o primeiro filho deles. As autoridades esperaram o bebê nascer e então levaram o recém-nascido ao pai, que estava preso. Disseram-lhe que agora era pai e que poderia voltar para casa e ficar com a esposa e o filho. Disseram que ele também poderia continuar a crer da mesma maneira, mas teria de ficar calado e não falar contra o pecado na igreja. O jovem pai se recusou, e por isso foi queimado na fogueira. Ficar calado não era uma opção.

Então, o que as Escrituras querem dizer com uma vida tranquila e pacífica? Paulo escreve a Timóteo: Exorto, pois, antes de tudo, que se façam súplicas, orações, intercessões e ações de graças por todos os homens; pelos reis e por todos os que exercem autoridade; para que levemos uma vida tranquila e pacífica, com toda piedade e honestidade. –1Tm 2:1-2. Pelos reis e por todos os que exercem autoridade, para que levemos uma vida tranquila e pacífica, com toda piedade e honestidade? Sim, o apóstolo Paulo diz isso, mas o que ele quis dizer? Será que quis dizer que devemos ficar calados a respeito do Evangelho? Ou que nunca devemos confrontar um pecador? Paulo não está nos dizendo para fazer algo que ele nunca fez, ou algo que o próprio Cristo nunca fez. Na verdade, as Escrituras revelam algo bem diferente.

Parece que os cristãos do Novo Testamento, tanto os da Bíblia quanto os da igreja primitiva, estavam ativamente espalhando o Evangelho e estavam entusiasmados com a Igreja de Jesus Cristo. Saíam pregando o Evangelho: realizavam reuniões nas montanhas, nos bosques ou em qualquer lugar aonde as pessoas fossem. Essa era a vida deles. Aqui, Paulo está dizendo que devemos orar para que, se estivermos obedecendo a Deus ao fazer coisas de que as autoridades não gostam, elas nos deixem em paz enquanto seguimos nossas atividades normais do dia a dia. Como cristãos, devemos espalhar a verdade da Palavra de Deus e agir ativamente para o avanço do Reino de Deus. Nossa oração deve ser para que as autoridades nos permitam viver em paz, enquanto servimos ao Príncipe da Paz.

Alguns cristãos tentam ser como o mundo em seus esforços para ganhar o mundo. Tentam convencer as pessoas a viver uma vida feliz, entrar para o nosso grupo, ser livres em Cristo, fazer uma viagem missionária emocionante, aproveitar a vida ao máximo, ser tudo o que puderem ser. Tudo gira em torno de “amar Jesus”, não de obedecer a ele.

E nós? Estamos entusiasmados para falar às pessoas sobre Jesus, mesmo que isso nos custe algo? Para muitos de nós é bastante fácil falar sobre agricultura, construção, caça ao veado e muitas outras coisas; no entanto, quando se trata das coisas de Deus, temos pouco a dizer. Temos tanto medo da perseguição? Tememos que o mundo nos odeie? Lembrem-se do que Jesus disse: Se o mundo vos odeia, sabei que primeiro me odiou a mim. Se fôsseis do mundo, o mundo amaria o que lhe pertence… –Jo 15:18-19. E: Portanto, qualquer que se envergonhar de mim e das minhas palavras nesta geração adúltera e pecadora, também dele o Filho do Homem se envergonhará, quando vier na glória de seu Pai com os santos anjos. –Mc 8:38

É fácil ser cristão quando você se instala e vive uma vida tranquila e pacífica, nunca desafiando um pecador, nunca corrigindo um irmão, nem jamais incomodando Satanás; mas quem disse que seria fácil? Aqui no Haiti, nós, como igreja, estamos tentando seguir Jesus, custe o que custar. Ainda ontem, dois membros nos disseram que estão prestes a perder o emprego por causa do Evangelho. Outra irmã da igreja contou que a escola onde seus filhos estudam exige uniformes e que as meninas precisam usar calças. Ela mandou a filha para a escola com um vestido modesto, mas a menina foi mandada de volta para casa com um bilhete da diretora dizendo que não deveria voltar à escola usando “aquela coisa”. Se sois insultados por causa do nome de Cristo, felizes sois, porque o Espírito da glória e de Deus repousa sobre vós; da parte deles, ele é blasfemado, mas da vossa parte é glorificado. –1Pe 4:14

A felicidade vem do sofrimento por causa da justiça. O sofrimento bíblico vem de obedecer a Jesus diante da oposição. Estamos ocupados demais discutindo opiniões pessoais sobre doutrina e tentando ser politicamente corretos, enquanto o mundo ri de nós e vai para o inferno? Sejamos como Jesus e como os cristãos fiéis ao longo dos séculos, vivendo de tal maneira que as pessoas ao nosso redor não possam negar que o poder de Deus está em nós. Temos algo de que todos precisam. Então, o que estamos esperando? Vamos nos reconciliar, reunir-nos novamente, negar a nós mesmos, tomar nossas cruzes e segui-lo!

And I sought for a man among them, that should make up the hedge, and stand in the gap before me for the land, that I should not destroy it: but I found none. –Ezekiel 22:30

The account of the little Dutch boy who heroically stuck his finger in the hole in the dike comes to mind as we consider such a verse. He couldn’t leave the spot for fear of erosion, so he waited the long night through until someone came along in the morning to rescue him from his plight. Many men have performed astounding feats on impulse when the moment so required. Lives were rescued, towns were saved, and enemies defeated because someone filled a role that was needed. Books are written, and monuments erected in honor of those whose benefaction has touched us. These are considered the heroes of history and they are remembered for their staunch bravery and steadfast faithfulness.

But the gaps in life are not always so obvious and the results not always measurable. Solomon informs us of the account of …a little city, and few men within it; and there came a great king against it, and besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it: Now there was found in it a poor wise man, and he by his wisdom delivered the city; yet no man remembered that same poor man. –Ecc 9:14-15. Though we have many thorough descriptions in the Bible of pious men who stood in the gap for God, there are, no doubt, hordes of others who overcame tremendous odds on a spiritual level yet received no recognition in this life.

The problem lies not so much in that, standing in the gap is beyond our capabilities or finances, but in the reality that often the job bears no title, ordination, or recognition. It is to be filled by volunteers with enough vision and care to sacrifice their own agenda for the sole cause of filling the hole in the hedge. It often does not lie within the realm of the physical, but within the borders of the spiritual. While the poor we have with us always and spiritual nobility will stoop to help them, we must consider that God probably has more in mind here than needing someone to organize bread lines and soup kitchens. He is looking for a man clad in a robe of “purple principles” that won’t be shed when the temperatures get hot.

King Darius signed the fateful degree that was designed to escort Daniel to a luncheon with the lions. Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime. –Dan 6:10. What a slight thing it would have been for Daniel to close the shutters before he prayed. But Daniel was not filling the gap by his presence in the high governmental position that he held. The gap lay in the dearth of godly witnesses in Babylon. Thus, the hole between heaven and earth was to be fulfilled by prayer at the open window while sacrificing his “seat in the senate.”

The underlying reason that so many gaps exist and there are so few men to fill them is because we often get our personal, earthly vision of circumstances confused with the eternal purposes of God. We are busily occupied with good things and feeling quite useful. Martha was zealously active in filling what she perceived as the imminent gap in the household, while Mary was sitting in the eternal one. It is incredibly easy to get caught up in the activity trap of a busy life. We may give intensive care to efficiently climb to the top of the ladder, only to discover that it is leaning against the wrong wall. Many people are very busy, but not very effective. Many have labored industriously for years in the Lord’s work, only to arrive at the finish line and realize that the things, which mattered most, had eluded them. Some, while giving their lives to serve others, allowed their marriage to suffer, or their children to disrespect them. Others have given “Corban” to their church while neglecting their relationship with their own parents.

The man in the gap must be wise, and wisdom must understand wherein the true gap lies. In this we must be driven by a purposed, biblical vision. Life will afford many opportunities to abandon our course. If we actively seek to live the expectations handed to us by our family, friends, associates, church agendas, and life’s circumstances, we will be driven by people rather than biblical principles. While this may seem legitimate on the surface, we may reap the bitter disappointment of finding ourselves dangling at the end of the wrong rope.

So, what does the gap of God’s concern look like? Some would say that this gap consists where any need arises. The poor we have with us always and certainly herein is an opportunity to do good. But the better part chosen by Mary had nothing to do with helping the poor or feeding the hungry. Likewise, the woman with the precious alabaster box of ointment of spikenard could have sold it and supplied the poor for quite a while with the sum of its value. But the real gap could not be filled by caressing the cripple, but by crowning the Christ. In the Garden of Eden there was no gap, for man walked in perfect harmony with his Creator. It was sin that created the gap and rankled the relationship. Also, there will be no breach at the end of time when the Lamb receives His bride. Until then, we have a large gap that exists because this earth refuses to glorify its Creator. To stand in that gap must be the chief purpose of all who aspire to bear His name.

This calls for a complete transformation in relationship to our God. The atonement of Christ’s blood makes it judicially possible. The comfort of the Holy Spirit makes it emotionally satisfying, but it is in the realm of our surrender and glorification of God that animates the scene. The Prodigal Son is a prime example of a soul who had brought a world of trouble upon himself by forsaking the position that he held as a son of his father. At the bottom of his restoration was nothing more than a re-establishing of the father-son relationship which had existed from his birth.

It appears to me that God is not so much looking for souls with their hands waving in the air shouting, “Here am I send me!” Rather His eyes search for the humble souls who bow their wills before the Almighty and recognize Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created. –Revelation 4:11. There is no lack for Sons of Sceva who imagine they are filling an important role in their willingness to broadcast the “Jesus” that they have heard of. In 1997, some 800,000 men arrived at a Promise Keepers rally in Washington D.C in response to the theme of “Standing in the Gap.” These men may have had good intentions of representing God to a nation in swift departure from spiritual underpinnings, but it takes more than just a willing heart. God doesn’t need of a large mass of bodies to stuff into a hole. He is looking for qualified men, and few have been promoted to such a position.

If all God wanted was men to show up at a rally or publicly proclaim their faith on the streets, He, no doubt, could have found many desiring such a good work. But to stand in the gap between God and the world will only be sanctioned by God for those who deserve to be there. It is the universal pride of man that drives man to believe that he must only desire to be useful and then he will be used. In God’s house there are some vessels to honor and some to dishonor, yet to deserve an honorable place is much more difficult than to desire one.

It is very common in our day to receive mail bearing the message, “Get the credit you deserve.” It is no secret that the credit that many deserve is zero credit. But we have all been impacted by the subliminal message that everybody deserves credit. Our society is promoting that all immoral, imprudent, and improvident people deserve the same care as the moral and industrious. If the slothful individual deserves a good wage and the spendthrift deserves financial security, then the Apostle Paul certainly has no right to lay any qualifications upon the widows who should receive support from the church. Neither has he any right to reject any sincere soul who desires the office of a Bishop, just because he does not meet the qualifications. But God noticed a few souls …in Sardis which have not defiled their garments; and they shall walk with me in white: for they are worthy. –Rev 3:4

These are men in the gap. Not because they had energy to burn, but because they had a vision for purity. This was no mere accident, for men who wish to attain to preeminence with God must do it by…

…Purpose

By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter; Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season; Esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt: for he had respect unto the recompence of the reward. By faith he forsook Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king: for he endured, as seeing him who is invisible. –Heb 11:24-27

A true vision for the work of God will come with a price tag. The rich young ruler would have loved to be a ruler in the kingdom of Christ as well as on his estate, but he couldn’t hold both. This principle provided the first hurdle for him and for everyone else who would desire such a noble work. As a young man, Moses made his decision and chose his loyalties. He was prepared to be rejected by Egypt, but he never dreamed he would also be so flippantly discarded by his own people.

It was forty years in the lonely furnace that purged his pride and pruned his prowess. There he graduated from the seminary of silence, equipped and prepared to stand in the gap as the meekest man on the face of the earth. He became an intercessor for men to God. As an advocate of men and of God, he preached and prayed, he walked and wept, he lived and loved his God and his brethren. All this while, he deemed himself inadequate for the position. While the children of Israel were at the very core of his heart, his fear and focus never left his God. When we seek to be respected by men, our purpose is clouded over and our position in the gap forfeited. Many good pastors, parents, and pilgrims have made this mistake and received their script from their wife, their children, their friends, or their church. Perhaps it seems like the loving, caring, and most respectful thing to do. But God requires absolute fidelity and there can be no compromise. What a man “wants to be” is driven by his visionary purpose, but what he “turns out to be” rests upon his…

…Priorities

This is a true saying, If a man desire the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work. A bishop then must be blameless, the husband of one wife, vigilant, sober, of good behaviour, given to hospitality, apt to teach; Not given to wine, no striker, not greedy of filthy lucre; but patient, not a brawler, not covetous; One that ruleth well his own house, having his children in subjection with all gravity; –1Ti 3:1-4. Our purpose forms our destination, but our priorities pave the road to get us there.

Unfortunately, some men are promoted to the ministry by popular opinion, but God chooses his men based upon their priorities and eternal qualifications. Men who are governed by their possessions, passions, or position will be useless to serve for God’s purpose. They love to be called Pastor, Reverend, or Father. They love to be esteemed as zealous, knowledgeable, steadfast, or compassionate. For am I now seeking the favor of men, or of God? Or am I striving to please men? If I were still pleasing men, I should not be a servant of Christ. –Gal 1:10 ASV

Fortunately, God is not a respecter of persons, and a stone fit for the wall will not be left in the way. The aged, the poor, the maimed, and the halt are all prime candidates for the position of filling the gap. Those with broken dreams, broken bodies, and broken hearts can stand unhindered in the hedge beside Noah, Abraham, Joseph, Moses, Daniel, Esther, Ruth and a countless battalion of others. These are all stellar representatives of God to this world. They all have turned their back on frivolity, fame, familiarity, and fortune and have become the heroes of heaven. They stand shoulder to shoulder in the hedge and form the “Embassy of the Eternal.” They loved, while others hated. They gave all, while others received. They were mocked and misunderstood, reviled and ridiculed, weary and weeping.

For we are unto God a sweet savour of Christ, in them that are saved, and in them that perish: To the one we are the savour of death unto death; and to the other the savour of life unto life. And who is sufficient for these things? –2 Co 2:15-16. Those whose sole purpose and priorities are governed by God.

״ואבקש מהם איש גודר גדר ועומד בפרץ לפני בעד הארץ לבלתי שחתה, ולא מצאתי.״ – יחזקאל 22:30

כשאנו מהרהרים בפסוק כזה, עולה בדעתנו הסיפור על הילד ההולנדי הקטן שתקע בגבורה את אצבעו בחור בסכר. הוא לא יכול היה לעזוב את המקום מחשש שהסכר ייסחף, ולכן המתין לאורך הלילה עד שמישהו עבר שם בבוקר וחילץ אותו ממצוקתו. גברים רבים חוללו מעשי גבורה מדהימים מתוך דחף של הרגע, כשהנסיבות דרשו זאת. אנשים ניצלו, עיירות נושעו ואויבים הובסו, משום שמישהו מילא תפקיד שהיה נחוץ. ספרים נכתבים ואנדרטאות מוקמות לכבוד מי שגמולם הטוב נגע בנו. הם נחשבים לגיבורי ההיסטוריה וזוכרים אותם בשל אומץ לבם האיתן ונאמנותם היציבה.

אבל הפרצות בחיים אינן תמיד ברורות כל כך, וגם את התוצאות לא תמיד אפשר למדוד. שלמה מספר לנו על ״עיר קטנה ואנשים בה מעט, ובא אליה מלך גדול וסבב אותה ובנה עליה מצודים גדולים. ומצא בה איש מסכן חכם, ומילט הוא את העיר בחכמתו, ואדם לא זכר את האיש המסכן ההוא.״ – קהלת 9:14-15. אף שיש בתנ״ך תיאורים מפורטים רבים של אנשים יראי אלוהים שעמדו בפרץ למענו, אין ספק שהיו המוני אחרים שהתגברו על מכשולים עצומים במישור הרוחני, ובכל זאת לא זכו להכרה בחייהם.

הבעיה אינה נעוצה כל כך בכך שעמידה בפרץ חורגת מיכולותינו או מיכולתנו הכלכלית, אלא בכך שלעתים קרובות אין לתפקיד הזה תואר, הסמכה או הכרה. על מתנדבים למלא אותו, אנשים בעלי חזון ואכפתיות במידה מספקת כדי להקריב את תוכניותיהם האישיות למען המטרה היחידה של סתימת הפרצה בגדר. לא פעם אין מדובר במישור הגשמי, אלא בתחום הרוחני. אמנם העניים תמיד יהיו איתנו, ואנשים בעלי אצילות רוחנית ישפילו את עצמם כדי לעזור להם, אך עלינו להביא בחשבון שאלוהים כנראה מתכוון כאן ליותר מהצורך במישהו שיארגן חלוקת לחם ומטבחים לנזקקים. הוא מחפש אדם העטוי בגלימה של ״עקרונות סגולים״, שלא תוסר כשהטמפרטורה תעלה.

המלך דריווש חתם על הצו הגורלי שנועד לשלוח את דניאל לארוחת צהריים עם האריות. ״וכדי ידע דניאל כי רשים כתבא, על לביתיה, וכוין פתיחן לה בעליתה נגד ירושלם, וזמנין תלתה ביומא הוא ברך על ברכוהי ומצלא ומודא קדם אלהה, כל קבל די הוא עבד מן קדמת דנה.״ – דניאל 6:10. איזה דבר פעוט היה זה אילו סגר דניאל את התריסים לפני שהתפלל. אבל דניאל לא מילא את הפרצה בכך שנכח בתפקיד הממשלתי הבכיר שבו כיהן. הפרצה הייתה המחסור בעדים יראי אלוהים בבבל. לכן היה עליו לסתום את הפער בין השמים לארץ באמצעות תפילה ליד החלון הפתוח, תוך הקרבת ״מושבו בסנאט״.

הסיבה הבסיסית לכך שיש כל כך הרבה פרצות וכל כך מעט אנשים שיסתמו אותן היא שלעתים קרובות אנו מבלבלים בין השקפתנו האישית והארצית על הנסיבות לבין מטרותיו הנצחיות של אלוהים. אנו עסוקים עד מעל לראש בדברים טובים ומרגישים מועילים למדי. מרתא פעלה בלהט כדי למלא את מה שראתה כצורך המיידי בבית, ואילו מרים ישבה לצד הנצחי. קל להפליא להילכד במלכודת העשייה של חיים עמוסים. אנו עלולים להשקיע טיפול מסור בטיפוס יעיל לראש הסולם, רק כדי לגלות שהוא נשען על הקיר הלא נכון. אנשים רבים עסוקים מאוד, אך אינם יעילים במיוחד. רבים עמלו בחריצות במשך שנים בעבודת האדון, ורק כשהגיעו לקו הסיום הבינו שהדברים החשובים ביותר חמקו מהם. יש שאפשרו לנישואיהם להיפגע או לילדיהם לא לכבד אותם, בשעה שהקדישו את חייהם לשירות הזולת. אחרים נתנו ״קורבן״ לכנסייה שלהם, ובה בעת הזניחו את יחסיהם עם הוריהם.

האדם העומד בפרץ חייב להיות חכם, ועל החוכמה להבין היכן נמצאת הפרצה האמיתית. בכך עלינו להיות מונחים בידי חזון מכוון המבוסס על התנ״ך. החיים יזמנו הזדמנויות רבות לנטוש את דרכנו. אם נבקש במרץ לעמוד בציפיות שמציבים בפנינו משפחתנו, חברינו, עמיתינו, סדרי העדיפויות של הכנסייה ונסיבות החיים, אנשים ינחו אותנו במקום עקרונות מקראיים. גם אם הדבר נראה לגיטימי על פניו, אנו עלולים לקטוף אכזבה מרה כשנגלה שאנחנו תלויים בקצה החבל הלא נכון.

אם כן, כיצד נראית הפרצה שאלוהים דואג לה? יש שיאמרו שהפרצה היא כל מקום שבו מתעורר צורך. העניים תמיד יהיו איתנו, ובהחלט יש כאן הזדמנות לעשות טוב. אבל לחלק הטוב יותר שבחרה מרים לא היה שום קשר לעזרה לעניים או להאכלת רעבים. בדומה לכך, האישה עם כלי הבושם היקר מאלבסטר ובו נרד הייתה יכולה למכור אותו ולספק את צורכי העניים במשך זמן רב בכסף שהתקבל תמורתו. אבל את הפרצה האמיתית אי אפשר למלא בליטוף הנכה, אלא בהכתרת המשיח. בגן עדן לא הייתה פרצה, כי האדם התהלך בהרמוניה מושלמת עם בוראו. החטא הוא שיצר את הפרצה ופגע ביחסים. כמו כן, לא יהיה עוד סדק באחרית הימים, כשהשה יקבל את כלתו. עד אז קיימת פרצה גדולה, משום שהארץ הזאת מסרבת לפאר את בוראה. עמידה בפרצה הזאת חייבת להיות מטרתם העיקרית של כל השואפים לשאת את שמו.

הדבר מחייב שינוי מוחלט ביחסינו עם אלוהים. כפרת דמו של המשיח מאפשרת זאת מבחינה משפטית. נחמת רוח הקודש מעניקה לכך סיפוק רגשי, אך ההתמסרות שלנו והאדרת אלוהים הן שמניעות את המתרחש. הבן האובד הוא דוגמה מובהקת לנפש שהמיטָה על עצמה צרות רבות כשנטשה את מעמדה כבן לאביו. יסוד השיקום שלו לא היה אלא חידוש היחסים בין האב לבן, שהתקיימו מאז לידתו.

נראה לי שאלוהים אינו מחפש בעיקר נפשות שמנופפות בידיהן באוויר וצועקות: ״הנני, שלח אותי!״ אלא עיניו מחפשות את הנפשות הענוות הכופפות את רצונן לפני האל הכול יכול ומכירות בכך: ״ראוי אתה, אדוננו ואלוהינו, לקבל את הכבוד ואת ההדר ואת הגבורה, כי אתה בראת את הכול וברצונך היו ונבראו.״ – ההתגלות 4:11. לא חסרים בני סווקי המדמים שהם ממלאים תפקיד חשוב בכך שהם מוכנים להפיץ את ״ישוע״ ששמעו עליו. בשנת 1997 הגיעו כ־800,000 גברים לעצרת של שומרי ההבטחה בוושינגטון הבירה, בתגובה לנושא ״עומדים בפרץ״. ייתכן שלגברים האלה היו כוונות טובות לייצג את אלוהים בפני אומה שמתרחקת במהירות מיסודותיה הרוחניים, אבל יותר מלב נכון נדרש לשם כך. אלוהים אינו זקוק להמון גדול של גופים שיידחסו לתוך פרצה. הוא מחפש גברים ראויים, ומעטים זכו לעלות לתפקיד כזה.

אילו כל מה שאלוהים רצה היה גברים שיבואו לעצרת או יכריזו בפומבי על אמונתם ברחובות, אין ספק שהיה יכול למצוא רבים החפצים במעשה טוב כזה. אבל עמידה בפרץ בין אלוהים לעולם תאושר בידי אלוהים רק למי שראויים לעמוד שם. גאוותו האוניברסלית של האדם היא שמניעה אותו להאמין שכל שעליו לעשות הוא לרצות להיות מועיל, ואז ישתמשו בו. בבית אלוהים יש כלים לכבוד וכלים לביזיון, אך להיות ראוי למקום של כבוד קשה הרבה יותר מלרצות בו.

בימינו נפוץ מאוד לקבל מכתבים הנושאים את המסר: ״קבלו את ההכרה המגיעה לכם״. אין זה סוד שההכרה שמגיעה לרבים היא אפס הכרה. ובכל זאת, כולנו הושפענו מהמסר הסמוי שלפיו לכולם מגיע קרדיט. החברה שלנו מקדמת את הרעיון שכל האנשים הלא מוסריים, חסרי התבונה והבזבזנים ראויים לאותה תמיכה כמו המוסריים והחרוצים. אם לעצלן מגיע שכר טוב ולבזבזן מגיע ביטחון כלכלי, הרי שלשליח פאולוס אין שום זכות להציב תנאי כשירות לאלמנות שצריכות לקבל תמיכה מהכנסייה. גם אין לו שום זכות לדחות נפש כנה החפצה בתפקיד המשגיח, רק משום שאינה עומדת בתנאי הכשירות. אבל אלוהים הבחין בכמה נפשות ״בסרדיס שלא טימאו את בגדיהם, והם ילכו איתי בלבן, כי ראויים הם לכך.״ – ההתגלות 3:4

אלה האנשים העומדים בפרץ. לא מפני שהיה להם מרץ להתבזבז, אלא מפני שהיה להם חזון של טוהר. הדבר לא קרה במקרה, שכן מי שרוצים להגיע למעמד בכיר בעיני אלוהים חייבים לעשות זאת באמצעות…

…תכלית

״באמונה סירב משה, כשגדל, להיקרא בן לבת פרעה. הוא בחר להתענות עם עם האלוהים מלהתענג לזמן קצר בתענוגות החטא, וחשב את חרפת המשיח לעושר גדול יותר מאוצרות מצרים, כי נשא עיניו אל הגמול. באמונה עזב את מצרים ולא ירא את זעם המלך, כי התחזק כאילו ראה את מי שאינו נראה.״ – אל העברים 11:24-27

לחזון אמיתי של עבודת אלוהים יש מחיר. השליט הצעיר והעשיר היה שמח להיות שליט גם במלכות המשיח וגם באחוזתו, אבל לא יכול היה להחזיק בשניהם. העיקרון הזה הציב בפניו ובפני כל מי שרצה בעבודה אצילית כזאת את המכשול הראשון. משה קיבל את החלטתו כצעיר ובחר את נאמנותו. הוא היה מוכן לכך שמצרים תדחה אותו, אך מעולם לא העלה בדעתו שעמו שלו יתנער ממנו בקלות דעת כזאת.

ארבעים השנים בכור ההיתוך הבודד טיהרו את גאוותו וריסנו את כוחו. שם סיים את הסמינר של הדממה, מצויד ומוכן לעמוד בפרץ כאיש העניו ביותר על פני האדמה. הוא נעשה למליץ יושר של בני אדם לפני אלוהים. כסנגורם של בני האדם ושל אלוהים, הוא הטיף והתפלל, הלך ובכה, חי ואהב את אלוהיו ואת אחיו. במשך כל הזמן הזה הוא ראה את עצמו בלתי כשיר לתפקיד. בני ישראל היו בלב לבו, אך פחדו ותשומת לבו לא משו מאלוהים. כשאנחנו מבקשים לזכות בכבודם של בני אדם, תכליתנו מתערפלת ואנו מוותרים על מקומנו בפרץ. כמרים, הורים ועולי רגל טובים רבים שגו כך וקיבלו את התסריט שלהם מאשתם, מילדיהם, מחבריהם או מכנסייתם. אולי נדמה שזה הדבר האוהב, המתחשב והמכבד ביותר לעשות. אבל אלוהים דורש נאמנות מוחלטת ואין מקום לפשרות. מה שאדם ״רוצה להיות״ מונע מתכלית החזון שלו, אך מה ש״יוצא ממנו להיות״ תלוי ב…

…סדרי עדיפויות

״נאמן הדבר: אם מישהו שואף לתפקיד משגיח, הוא חושק בעבודה טובה. לכן על המשגיח להיות ללא דופי, בעל אישה אחת, מפוכח, שקול, הגון, מכניס אורחים ומוכשר ללמד; לא שתיין ולא אלים, לא רודף בצע, אלא סבלני, לא מתקוטט ולא אוהב כסף; מנהיג היטב את ביתו שלו ומחזיק את ילדיו תחת מרות בכובד ראש;״ – טימותיאוס א׳ 3:1-4. תכליתנו מעצבת את יעדנו, אך סדרי העדיפויות שלנו סוללים את הדרך אליו.

למרבה הצער, יש גברים שמקודמים לתפקיד בשירות הדתי מכוח דעת הקהל, אך אלוהים בוחר את אנשיו על פי סדרי העדיפויות שלהם והתנאים הנצחיים. אנשים הנשלטים בידי רכושם, תשוקותיהם או מעמדם לא יועילו לשירות מטרתו של אלוהים. הם אוהבים שיקראו להם כומר, כבוד האב או אב. הם אוהבים שיחשיבו אותם לקנאים, יודעי דבר, איתנים או רחומים. ״האם אני מבקש עכשיו את חסדם של בני אדם או את חסדו של אלוהים? האם אני משתדל למצוא חן בעיני בני אדם? אילו עדיין הייתי מבקש למצוא חן בעיני בני אדם, לא הייתי עבד המשיח.״ – גלטים 1:10 ASV

למרבה המזל, אלוהים אינו נושא פנים, ואבן המתאימה לחומה לא תישאר מונחת בצד. זקנים, עניים, בעלי מום ופיסחים הם כולם מועמדים ראויים למילוי הפרצה. בעלי חלומות שבורים, גופים שבורים ולבבות שבורים יכולים לעמוד ללא הפרעה בגדר לצד נוח, אברהם, יוסף, משה, דניאל, אסתר, רות וגדוד אין־ספור של אחרים. כולם נציגים נבחרים של אלוהים בעולם הזה. כולם הפנו גבם להבלים, לתהילה, לנוחות ולהון והיו לגיבורי השמים. הם עומדים כתף אל כתף בגדר ויוצרים את ״שגרירות הנצח״. הם אהבו בזמן שאחרים שנאו. הם נתנו הכול בזמן שאחרים קיבלו. לעגו להם ולא הבינו אותם, חרפו וגידפו אותם, והם היו עייפים ובוכיים.

״כי ריח ניחוח המשיח אנחנו לאלוהים, בין הנושעים ובין האובדים: לאלה ריח מוות למוות, ולאלה ריח חיים לחיים. ומי ראוי לדברים האלה?״ – קורינתים ב׳ 2:15-16. אלה שתכליתם היחידה וסדרי העדיפויות שלהם מונהגים בידי אלוהים.

Mile after mile sped by as Carol drove the old Chevy along the busy interstate highway toward home. Between intervals of silence and conversation, Carol and her two sisters, Elaine and Gloria, lifted their voices in song, giving thanks and praise to their Creator. How thankful they were for the opportunity to spend the evening with their friends at Pine Creek Church and to receive another inspiring message from God’s Word.

Suddenly their smooth travel was interrupted by signs of trouble. “Now what can be wrong with this car?” Carol worried out loud as she guided the stalled car to the side of the road. “Oh, no, girls, we’re out of gas! I was in such a hurry this evening that I forgot to check the gauge. I thought the tank was almost full when we left home, and… Oh no!” wailed Carol again. “Dad put the cell phone on the counter for me to take along, and I forgot that also!”

“Whatever are we going to do now?” exclaimed Elaine. “Here we are, stranded in the dark, no gas, no phone, and seven more miles to our exit! And another thing, people just don’t stop very quickly these days and offer help. They know that most everyone carries a phone. This seems almost impossible to me!” she mournfully uttered from the back seat.

As the girls lapsed into silence, the old Chevy seemed to shake in protest as a long row of trucks whizzed by. “You know,” said Gloria, “I was just remembering Brother Lester’s message this evening. How can we forget so quickly! Maybe God has allowed this to happen to us so our faith might be increased as we place our trust in Him. Let’s take this to the Lord in prayer. Let’s look for a miracle from God’s hand.”

Together the girls bowed their heads and pled for the Lord’s protection and help.

“You know, I feel better already,” smiled Elaine. “I was so worried and fearful, but since we prayed and committed everything to God, I have confidence that He will watch over us. I’m so glad we have a God who hears all of our cries. What would we do without His comforting Holy Spirit? Let’s sing again.”

“Joys are flowing like a river,
Since the Comforter has come;
He abides with us forever,
Makes the trusting heart His home.
Blessed quietness, holy quietness,
Blest assurance in my soul!
On the stormy sea Jesus speaks to me,
And the billows cease to roll!”

-Manie P. Ferguson, 19th century

As the girls sang song after song, their hearts were deeply stirred. How quiet and peaceful they felt, even though they were stranded on a dark highway thirteen miles from home. Car after car, and truck after truck sped by without stopping. Then they noticed a pickup truck, with two dirt bikes on the back, slowing down. It pulled off the road several hundred feet ahead of them, and slowly began to back up. The girls’ voices were stilled in silence as they desperately cried out to God from the bottom of their hearts. When the truck came to a halt, two husky, long-haired men jumped out. Carol rolled her window down as a man wearing a red-checked flannel jacket approached.

“What’s the trouble here, girls?” he asked, glancing over the car.

“We’re out of gas,” Carol quickly replied.

“Well, I’d say we’re pretty lucky. We have a can of gas with us. How far do you need to go yet?”

“About thirteen miles.”

“Good. We’ll just pour some of our gas into your tank and you can be on your way again. No payment necessary.”

“O thank you so much,” responded Carol. “We were praying that God would send us help, and He did more than we could ever have thought! Thanks so much.”

“Yes, yes”, replied the man gruffly, “You’re pretty lucky we came along. We’re just glad to help you out.”

Several minutes later, the girls were on their way again. “You know,” said Carol, “when I saw that truck pull over, I was scared and glad at the same time. I began to scold myself again for not having that cell phone with me. But then I asked God to help me completely trust in Him and not be afraid. After all, isn’t He much more dependable than any cell phone? This has been such a faith booster for me. How different this may have turned out, if we had depended solely on our cell phones or “good luck” as those men called it. It must grieve our Father’s heart tremendously when we do not place our trust in Him.”

“It’s just as Brother Lester preached this evening”, added Gloria. “Remember some of those verses? I waited patiently for the LORD; and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry … And he hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God… Blessed is that man that maketh the LORD his trust, and respecteth not the proud, nor such as turn aside to lies. –Psa 40:1-4. This makes me so happy I just want to keep singing and thanking the Lord!”

Again, the girls raised their voices in song:

“His eye is always watching,
His ear is keen to hear;
His love is all-sufficient
To calm the gravest fear.
Then trust Him in shine and shade;
Trust Him, be not afraid:
He’s walking close beside thee;
His hand will safely guide thee;
His wings securely hide thee;
Then trust! Be not afraid.”

-Charles H. Gabriel, 1856-1932

घर की ओर व्यस्त अंतरराज्यीय राजमार्ग पर पुरानी शेवी चलाते हुए कैरल के साथ मील-पर-मील पीछे छूटते गए। खामोशी और बातचीत के बीच, कैरल और उसकी दो बहनों, इलेन और ग्लोरिया, ने गीत गाते हुए अपने सृजनहार का धन्यवाद और स्तुति की। वे कितनी आभारी थीं कि उन्हें पाइन क्रीक चर्च में अपने मित्रों के साथ शाम बिताने और परमेश्वर के वचन से एक और प्रेरणादायक संदेश सुनने का अवसर मिला।

अचानक उनकी सहज यात्रा में परेशानी के संकेत आ गए। “अब इस गाड़ी में क्या गड़बड़ हो सकती है?” रुकी हुई गाड़ी को सड़क के किनारे ले जाते हुए कैरल ने चिंता से ज़ोर से कहा। “अरे नहीं, लड़कियो, पेट्रोल खत्म हो गया! आज शाम मुझे इतनी जल्दी थी कि मापक देखना ही भूल गई। मुझे लगा था कि घर से निकलते समय टंकी लगभग भरी हुई थी, और… अरे नहीं!” कैरल फिर विलाप करते हुए बोली। “पिताजी ने मेरे साथ ले जाने के लिए मोबाइल फ़ोन काउंटर पर रखा था, और मैं वह भी भूल गई!”

“अब हम क्या करने वाली हैं?” इलेन ने हैरानी से कहा। “हम यहाँ अँधेरे में फँसी हुई हैं, पेट्रोल नहीं, फ़ोन नहीं, और हमारे निकास तक सात मील और जाना है! और एक बात, आजकल लोग जल्दी रुककर मदद की पेशकश नहीं करते। उन्हें पता है कि लगभग हर किसी के पास फ़ोन होता है। यह बात मुझे लगभग नामुमकिन-सी लगती है!” उसने पिछली सीट से उदासी से कहा।

जब लड़कियाँ चुप हो गईं, तो पुरानी शेवी विरोध जताने की तरह हिलती हुई लगी, जबकि ट्रकों की एक लंबी कतार तेज़ी से गुज़र गई। “जानती हो,” ग्लोरिया ने कहा, “अभी मुझे आज शाम भाई लेस्टर का संदेश याद आ रहा था। हम इतनी जल्दी कैसे भूल सकते हैं! शायद परमेश्वर ने ऐसा होने दिया है ताकि उस पर भरोसा रखने से हमारा विश्वास बढ़े। आओ, यह बात प्रार्थना में प्रभु के सामने रखें। परमेश्वर के हाथ से चमत्कार की आशा करें।”

लड़कियों ने साथ-साथ सिर झुकाया और प्रभु से सुरक्षा तथा सहायता की विनती की।

“जानती हो, अब मुझे पहले से ही अच्छा लग रहा है,” इलेन मुस्कराई। “मैं बहुत चिंतित और डरी हुई थी, लेकिन जब से हमने प्रार्थना करके सब कुछ परमेश्वर को सौंप दिया है, मुझे भरोसा है कि वह हमारी देखभाल करेगा। मुझे कितनी खुशी है कि हमारा परमेश्वर हमारी हर पुकार सुनता है। उसकी दिलासा देने वाली पवित्र आत्मा के बिना हम क्या करते? आओ, फिर से गाएँ।”

“आनंद नदी-सा बहता है,
जब से दिलासा देने वाला आया;
वह सदा हमारे साथ रहता है,
विश्वास रखने वाले हृदय को अपना घर बनाता है।
धन्य शांति, पवित्र शांति,
मेरी आत्मा में धन्य आश्वासन!
तूफ़ानी सागर पर यीशु मुझसे बोलता है,
और लहरों का उफनना थम जाता है!”

-मैनी पी. फ़र्ग्यूसन, उन्नीसवीं शताब्दी

एक के बाद एक गीत गाते हुए लड़कियों के हृदय गहराई से स्पंदित हो उठे। वे कितनी शांत और सुकून में थीं, हालाँकि अँधेरे राजमार्ग पर घर से तेरह मील दूर फँसी हुई थीं। एक के बाद एक कार और ट्रक बिना रुके तेज़ी से निकलते गए। तभी उन्होंने देखा कि एक पिकअप ट्रक, जिसके पीछे दो डर्ट बाइक थीं, धीमा हो रहा है। वह उनसे कई सौ फ़ीट आगे सड़क से हटकर रुका और धीरे-धीरे पीछे आने लगा। परमेश्वर से पूरे हृदय से सहायता की गुहार लगाते हुए लड़कियों की आवाज़ें थम गईं। ट्रक रुकते ही, लंबे बालों वाले दो हट्टे-कट्टे आदमी बाहर कूदे। लाल चौखानेदार फलालैन की जैकेट पहने एक आदमी पास आया तो कैरल ने खिड़की नीचे कर दी।

“लड़कियो, यहाँ क्या परेशानी है?” उसने गाड़ी पर नज़र डालते हुए पूछा।

“हमारा पेट्रोल खत्म हो गया है,” कैरल ने तुरंत जवाब दिया।

“तो, मैं कहूँगा कि हमारी किस्मत अच्छी है। हमारे पास पेट्रोल का एक कनस्तर है। आपको अभी कितनी दूर जाना है?”

“लगभग तेरह मील।”

“अच्छा। हम अपने कनस्तर का थोड़ा पेट्रोल आपकी टंकी में डाल देंगे और आप फिर से चल पड़ेंगी। पैसे देने की ज़रूरत नहीं।”

“ओह, आपका बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद,” कैरल ने जवाब दिया। “हम प्रार्थना कर रही थीं कि परमेश्वर हमारी मदद के लिए किसी को भेजे, और उसने हमारी कल्पना से कहीं बढ़कर किया! बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद।”

“हाँ, हाँ,” आदमी ने रूखेपन से जवाब दिया, “आपकी किस्मत अच्छी थी कि हम आ गए। हमें बस आपकी मदद करके खुशी हुई।”

कुछ मिनट बाद लड़कियाँ फिर से रास्ते पर थीं। “जानती हो,” कैरल ने कहा, “जब मैंने उस ट्रक को सड़क किनारे रुकते देखा, तो मैं एक साथ डरी भी और खुश भी हुई। मेरे साथ मोबाइल फ़ोन न होने पर मैं फिर खुद को कोसने लगी। लेकिन फिर मैंने परमेश्वर से विनती की कि वह पूरी तरह उस पर भरोसा रखने और न डरने में मेरी मदद करे। आख़िर, क्या वह किसी भी मोबाइल फ़ोन से कहीं अधिक भरोसेमंद नहीं है? इससे मेरा विश्वास बहुत बढ़ा है। अगर हम केवल अपने मोबाइल फ़ोन या उन आदमियों के कहे ‘अच्छे भाग्य’ पर निर्भर रहतीं, तो न जाने यह सब कितना अलग होता। जब हम उस पर भरोसा नहीं रखते, तो इससे हमारे पिता का हृदय कितना दुखी होता होगा।”

“आज शाम भाई लेस्टर ने भी यही उपदेश दिया था,” ग्लोरिया ने आगे कहा। “उनमें से कुछ पद याद हैं? मैं धीरज से यहोवा की बाट जोहता रहा; और उसने मेरी ओर झुककर मेरी दोहाई सुनी… उसने मेरे मुँह में एक नया गीत, अर्थात् हमारे परमेश्वर की स्तुति का गीत, डाल दिया… धन्य है वह मनुष्य जो यहोवा पर भरोसा रखता है, और अभिमानियों की ओर नहीं फिरता, और न झूठ की ओर भटकने वालों की ओर। –भजन 40:1-4। इससे मुझे इतनी खुशी हो रही है कि मेरा मन बस गाते रहने और प्रभु का धन्यवाद करते रहने को करता है!”

लड़कियों ने फिर से गीत गाने के लिए अपनी आवाज़ें उठाईं:

“उसकी आँखें सदा निगाह रखती हैं,
उसका कान सुनने को तत्पर है;
उसका प्रेम सब कुछ सँभालने को पर्याप्त है,
सबसे गहरे भय को शांत करने के लिए।
फिर धूप हो या छाया, उस पर भरोसा रखो;
उस पर भरोसा रखो, मत डरो:
वह तुम्हारे बिलकुल पास चल रहा है;
उसका हाथ तुम्हारी सुरक्षित अगुवाई करेगा;
उसके पंख तुम्हें सुरक्षित छिपाएँगे;
इसलिए भरोसा रखो! मत डरो।”

-चार्ल्स एच. गैब्रियल, 1856-1932

And I sought for a man among them, that should make up the hedge, and stand in the gap before me for the land, that I should not destroy it: but I found none. –Ezekiel 22:30

The account of the little Dutch boy who heroically stuck his finger in the hole in the dike comes to mind as we consider such a verse. He couldn’t leave the spot for fear of erosion, so he waited the long night through until someone came along in the morning to rescue him from his plight. Many men have performed astounding feats on impulse when the moment so required. Lives were rescued, towns were saved, and enemies defeated because someone filled a role that was needed. Books are written, and monuments erected in honor of those whose benefaction has touched us. These are considered the heroes of history and they are remembered for their staunch bravery and steadfast faithfulness.

But the gaps in life are not always so obvious and the results not always measurable. Solomon informs us of the account of …a little city, and few men within it; and there came a great king against it, and besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it: Now there was found in it a poor wise man, and he by his wisdom delivered the city; yet no man remembered that same poor man. –Ecc 9:14-15. Though we have many thorough descriptions in the Bible of pious men who stood in the gap for God, there are, no doubt, hordes of others who overcame tremendous odds on a spiritual level yet received no recognition in this life.

The problem lies not so much in that, standing in the gap is beyond our capabilities or finances, but in the reality that often the job bears no title, ordination, or recognition. It is to be filled by volunteers with enough vision and care to sacrifice their own agenda for the sole cause of filling the hole in the hedge. It often does not lie within the realm of the physical, but within the borders of the spiritual. While the poor we have with us always and spiritual nobility will stoop to help them, we must consider that God probably has more in mind here than needing someone to organize bread lines and soup kitchens. He is looking for a man clad in a robe of “purple principles” that won’t be shed when the temperatures get hot.

King Darius signed the fateful degree that was designed to escort Daniel to a luncheon with the lions. Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime. –Dan 6:10. What a slight thing it would have been for Daniel to close the shutters before he prayed. But Daniel was not filling the gap by his presence in the high governmental position that he held. The gap lay in the dearth of godly witnesses in Babylon. Thus, the hole between heaven and earth was to be fulfilled by prayer at the open window while sacrificing his “seat in the senate.”

The underlying reason that so many gaps exist and there are so few men to fill them is because we often get our personal, earthly vision of circumstances confused with the eternal purposes of God. We are busily occupied with good things and feeling quite useful. Martha was zealously active in filling what she perceived as the imminent gap in the household, while Mary was sitting in the eternal one. It is incredibly easy to get caught up in the activity trap of a busy life. We may give intensive care to efficiently climb to the top of the ladder, only to discover that it is leaning against the wrong wall. Many people are very busy, but not very effective. Many have labored industriously for years in the Lord’s work, only to arrive at the finish line and realize that the things, which mattered most, had eluded them. Some, while giving their lives to serve others, allowed their marriage to suffer, or their children to disrespect them. Others have given “Corban” to their church while neglecting their relationship with their own parents.

The man in the gap must be wise, and wisdom must understand wherein the true gap lies. In this we must be driven by a purposed, biblical vision. Life will afford many opportunities to abandon our course. If we actively seek to live the expectations handed to us by our family, friends, associates, church agendas, and life’s circumstances, we will be driven by people rather than biblical principles. While this may seem legitimate on the surface, we may reap the bitter disappointment of finding ourselves dangling at the end of the wrong rope.

So, what does the gap of God’s concern look like? Some would say that this gap consists where any need arises. The poor we have with us always and certainly herein is an opportunity to do good. But the better part chosen by Mary had nothing to do with helping the poor or feeding the hungry. Likewise, the woman with the precious alabaster box of ointment of spikenard could have sold it and supplied the poor for quite a while with the sum of its value. But the real gap could not be filled by caressing the cripple, but by crowning the Christ. In the Garden of Eden there was no gap, for man walked in perfect harmony with his Creator. It was sin that created the gap and rankled the relationship. Also, there will be no breach at the end of time when the Lamb receives His bride. Until then, we have a large gap that exists because this earth refuses to glorify its Creator. To stand in that gap must be the chief purpose of all who aspire to bear His name.

This calls for a complete transformation in relationship to our God. The atonement of Christ’s blood makes it judicially possible. The comfort of the Holy Spirit makes it emotionally satisfying, but it is in the realm of our surrender and glorification of God that animates the scene. The Prodigal Son is a prime example of a soul who had brought a world of trouble upon himself by forsaking the position that he held as a son of his father. At the bottom of his restoration was nothing more than a re-establishing of the father-son relationship which had existed from his birth.

It appears to me that God is not so much looking for souls with their hands waving in the air shouting, “Here am I send me!” Rather His eyes search for the humble souls who bow their wills before the Almighty and recognize Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created. –Revelation 4:11. There is no lack for Sons of Sceva who imagine they are filling an important role in their willingness to broadcast the “Jesus” that they have heard of. In 1997, some 800,000 men arrived at a Promise Keepers rally in Washington D.C in response to the theme of “Standing in the Gap.” These men may have had good intentions of representing God to a nation in swift departure from spiritual underpinnings, but it takes more than just a willing heart. God doesn’t need of a large mass of bodies to stuff into a hole. He is looking for qualified men, and few have been promoted to such a position.

If all God wanted was men to show up at a rally or publicly proclaim their faith on the streets, He, no doubt, could have found many desiring such a good work. But to stand in the gap between God and the world will only be sanctioned by God for those who deserve to be there. It is the universal pride of man that drives man to believe that he must only desire to be useful and then he will be used. In God’s house there are some vessels to honor and some to dishonor, yet to deserve an honorable place is much more difficult than to desire one.

It is very common in our day to receive mail bearing the message, “Get the credit you deserve.” It is no secret that the credit that many deserve is zero credit. But we have all been impacted by the subliminal message that everybody deserves credit. Our society is promoting that all immoral, imprudent, and improvident people deserve the same care as the moral and industrious. If the slothful individual deserves a good wage and the spendthrift deserves financial security, then the Apostle Paul certainly has no right to lay any qualifications upon the widows who should receive support from the church. Neither has he any right to reject any sincere soul who desires the office of a Bishop, just because he does not meet the qualifications. But God noticed a few souls …in Sardis which have not defiled their garments; and they shall walk with me in white: for they are worthy. –Rev 3:4

These are men in the gap. Not because they had energy to burn, but because they had a vision for purity. This was no mere accident, for men who wish to attain to preeminence with God must do it by…

…Purpose

By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter; Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season; Esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt: for he had respect unto the recompence of the reward. By faith he forsook Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king: for he endured, as seeing him who is invisible. –Heb 11:24-27

A true vision for the work of God will come with a price tag. The rich young ruler would have loved to be a ruler in the kingdom of Christ as well as on his estate, but he couldn’t hold both. This principle provided the first hurdle for him and for everyone else who would desire such a noble work. As a young man, Moses made his decision and chose his loyalties. He was prepared to be rejected by Egypt, but he never dreamed he would also be so flippantly discarded by his own people.

It was forty years in the lonely furnace that purged his pride and pruned his prowess. There he graduated from the seminary of silence, equipped and prepared to stand in the gap as the meekest man on the face of the earth. He became an intercessor for men to God. As an advocate of men and of God, he preached and prayed, he walked and wept, he lived and loved his God and his brethren. All this while, he deemed himself inadequate for the position. While the children of Israel were at the very core of his heart, his fear and focus never left his God. When we seek to be respected by men, our purpose is clouded over and our position in the gap forfeited. Many good pastors, parents, and pilgrims have made this mistake and received their script from their wife, their children, their friends, or their church. Perhaps it seems like the loving, caring, and most respectful thing to do. But God requires absolute fidelity and there can be no compromise. What a man “wants to be” is driven by his visionary purpose, but what he “turns out to be” rests upon his…

…Priorities

This is a true saying, If a man desire the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work. A bishop then must be blameless, the husband of one wife, vigilant, sober, of good behaviour, given to hospitality, apt to teach; Not given to wine, no striker, not greedy of filthy lucre; but patient, not a brawler, not covetous; One that ruleth well his own house, having his children in subjection with all gravity; –1Ti 3:1-4. Our purpose forms our destination, but our priorities pave the road to get us there.

Unfortunately, some men are promoted to the ministry by popular opinion, but God chooses his men based upon their priorities and eternal qualifications. Men who are governed by their possessions, passions, or position will be useless to serve for God’s purpose. They love to be called Pastor, Reverend, or Father. They love to be esteemed as zealous, knowledgeable, steadfast, or compassionate. For am I now seeking the favor of men, or of God? Or am I striving to please men? If I were still pleasing men, I should not be a servant of Christ. –Gal 1:10 ASV

Fortunately, God is not a respecter of persons, and a stone fit for the wall will not be left in the way. The aged, the poor, the maimed, and the halt are all prime candidates for the position of filling the gap. Those with broken dreams, broken bodies, and broken hearts can stand unhindered in the hedge beside Noah, Abraham, Joseph, Moses, Daniel, Esther, Ruth and a countless battalion of others. These are all stellar representatives of God to this world. They all have turned their back on frivolity, fame, familiarity, and fortune and have become the heroes of heaven. They stand shoulder to shoulder in the hedge and form the “Embassy of the Eternal.” They loved, while others hated. They gave all, while others received. They were mocked and misunderstood, reviled and ridiculed, weary and weeping.

For we are unto God a sweet savour of Christ, in them that are saved, and in them that perish: To the one we are the savour of death unto death; and to the other the savour of life unto life. And who is sufficient for these things? –2 Co 2:15-16. Those whose sole purpose and priorities are governed by God.

Ik zocht onder hen iemand die de muur zou kunnen herstellen en voor Mij in de bres zou staan voor het land, zodat Ik het niet hoefde te vernietigen, maar Ik vond niemand. –Ezechiël 22:30

Wanneer we zo’n vers overdenken, denken we aan het verhaal van het kleine Nederlandse jongetje dat heldhaftig zijn vinger in het gat in de dijk stak. Uit angst voor erosie kon hij niet van zijn plek weggaan, dus wachtte hij de lange nacht door totdat er ’s morgens iemand langskwam om hem uit zijn benarde situatie te redden. Veel mannen hebben op het moment dat het nodig was impulsief verbazingwekkende prestaties geleverd. Levens werden gered, steden werden behouden en vijanden verslagen omdat iemand een noodzakelijke rol vervulde. Er worden boeken geschreven en monumenten opgericht ter ere van hen wier verdiensten ons hebben geraakt. Zij worden beschouwd als de helden van de geschiedenis en herinnerd om hun standvastige moed en onwankelbare trouw.

Maar de gaten in het leven zijn niet altijd zo duidelijk en de resultaten zijn niet altijd meetbaar. Salomo vertelt ons het verhaal van …een kleine stad met weinig inwoners; er kwam een groot koning op haar af, omsingelde haar en bouwde grote belegeringswerken tegen haar. Nu bevond zich in die stad een arme, wijze man, en die redde de stad door zijn wijsheid; toch herinnerde niemand zich die arme man. –Pred 9:14-15. Hoewel de Bijbel ons veel uitvoerige beschrijvingen geeft van godvruchtige mannen die voor God in de bres stonden, zijn er ongetwijfeld talloze anderen die op geestelijk vlak enorme hindernissen overwonnen, maar in dit leven geen erkenning kregen.

Het probleem is niet zozeer dat in de bres staan onze mogelijkheden of middelen te boven gaat, maar dat het werk vaak geen titel, wijding of erkenning met zich meebrengt. Het moet worden gedaan door vrijwilligers met voldoende inzicht en toewijding om hun eigen agenda op te offeren voor het enige doel: het gat in de omheining te vullen. Vaak gaat het niet om het fysieke, maar om het geestelijke. Hoewel wij de armen altijd bij ons hebben en geestelijke edelen zich zullen bukken om hen te helpen, moeten we bedenken dat God hier waarschijnlijk meer op het oog heeft dan iemand die voedseluitdelingen en gaarkeukens organiseert. Hij zoekt een man gehuld in een gewaad van ‘paarse principes’ dat niet wordt afgelegd wanneer de temperaturen oplopen.

Koning Darius ondertekende het noodlottige decreet dat Daniël naar een lunch met de leeuwen zou sturen. Toen Daniël wist dat het geschrift ondertekend was, ging hij naar zijn huis. In zijn bovenkamer waren de vensters open in de richting van Jeruzalem. Hij knielde drie keer per dag op zijn knieën, bad en dankte zijn God, zoals hij vroeger ook deed. –Dan 6:10. Wat een kleinigheid zou het voor Daniël zijn geweest om de luiken te sluiten voordat hij bad. Maar Daniël vulde de bres niet door zijn aanwezigheid in de hoge regeringsfunctie die hij bekleedde. De bres bestond uit het gebrek aan godvruchtige getuigen in Babylon. Zo moest het gat tussen hemel en aarde worden gevuld door bij het open raam te bidden, terwijl hij zijn ‘zetel in de senaat’ op het spel zette.

De onderliggende reden dat er zoveel bressen zijn en zo weinig mannen om ze te vullen, is dat we ons persoonlijke, aardse beeld van de omstandigheden vaak verwarren met Gods eeuwige bedoelingen. We zijn druk bezig met goede dingen en voelen ons heel nuttig. Martha was ijverig bezig de dreigende leemte in het huishouden te vullen zoals zij die zag, terwijl Maria plaatsnam in de eeuwige. Het is verbazingwekkend gemakkelijk om verstrikt te raken in de activiteitenval van een druk leven. We kunnen ons intensief inspannen om efficiënt de top van de ladder te bereiken, om vervolgens te ontdekken dat die tegen de verkeerde muur staat. Veel mensen zijn erg druk, maar niet erg doeltreffend. Velen hebben jarenlang ijverig in het werk van de Heer gezwoegd, om bij de finish te ontdekken dat ze de dingen die er het meest toe deden uit het oog waren verloren. Sommigen lieten, terwijl ze hun leven gaven om anderen te dienen, hun huwelijk lijden of stonden toe dat hun kinderen hen niet respecteerden. Anderen hebben ‘Korban’ aan hun kerk gegeven, terwijl ze hun relatie met hun eigen ouders verwaarloosden.

De man in de bres moet wijs zijn, en wijsheid moet begrijpen waar de werkelijke bres ligt. Daarbij moeten we ons laten leiden door een doelgerichte, bijbelse visie. Het leven biedt veel kansen om onze koers te verlaten. Als we actief proberen te voldoen aan de verwachtingen die onze familie, vrienden, kennissen, kerkelijke agenda’s en levensomstandigheden ons opleggen, zullen we ons door mensen laten leiden in plaats van door bijbelse beginselen. Hoewel dat aan de oppervlakte redelijk kan lijken, kunnen we de bittere teleurstelling oogsten dat we aan het verkeerde touw bungelen.

Hoe ziet de bres eruit waarover God zich zorgen maakt? Sommigen zeggen dat deze bres ontstaat wanneer er maar enige nood is. De armen hebben we altijd bij ons en daar ligt beslist een gelegenheid om goed te doen. Maar het betere deel dat Maria koos, had niets te maken met de armen helpen of de hongerigen voeden. Evenzo had de vrouw met de kostbare albasten kruik met nardusolie die kunnen verkopen en de armen met de opbrengst geruime tijd kunnen onderhouden. Maar de werkelijke bres kon niet worden gevuld door de verlamde liefdevol te omhelzen, maar door Christus te kronen. In de hof van Eden was er geen bres, want de mens wandelde in volmaakte harmonie met zijn Schepper. De zonde schiep de bres en verstoorde de relatie. Ook zal er aan het einde der tijden geen breuk zijn wanneer het Lam Zijn bruid ontvangt. Tot die tijd bestaat er een grote bres, omdat deze aarde weigert haar Schepper te verheerlijken. In die bres staan moet het voornaamste doel zijn van allen die ernaar streven Zijn naam te dragen.

Dit vraagt om een volledige verandering in onze relatie met God. De verzoening door het bloed van Christus maakt dit juridisch mogelijk. De troost van de Heilige Geest maakt het emotioneel bevredigend, maar het is het terrein van onze overgave en verheerlijking van God dat de scène tot leven brengt. De verloren zoon is een treffend voorbeeld van iemand die zichzelf een wereld aan ellende had bezorgd door de positie te verzaken die hij als zoon van zijn vader innam. De kern van zijn herstel was niets anders dan het opnieuw tot stand brengen van de vader-zoonrelatie die vanaf zijn geboorte had bestaan.

Het lijkt mij dat God niet zozeer zoekt naar mensen die met hun handen in de lucht zwaaien en roepen: ‘Hier ben ik, zend mij!’ Zijn ogen zoeken veeleer de nederige mensen die hun wil buigen voor de Almachtige en erkennen: U bent waardig, o Heer, om de heerlijkheid, de eer en de kracht te ontvangen, want U hebt alle dingen geschapen en door Uw wil bestaan zij en zijn zij geschapen. –Openbaring 4:11. Er is geen gebrek aan zonen van Sceva die denken dat ze een belangrijke rol vervullen door bereidwillig de ‘Jezus’ rond te bazuinen over wie ze hebben gehoord. In 1997 kwamen ongeveer 800.000 mannen bijeen bij een Promise Keepers-rally in Washington D.C. als reactie op het thema ‘In de bres staan’. Deze mannen hadden misschien goede bedoelingen: God vertegenwoordigen tegenover een natie die zich snel van haar geestelijke fundamenten verwijderde. Maar meer dan alleen een bereidwillig hart is nodig. God heeft geen grote massa lichamen nodig om een gat op te vullen. Hij zoekt geschikte mannen, en slechts weinigen zijn tot zo’n positie bevorderd.

Als God alleen maar wilde dat mannen naar een bijeenkomst kwamen of in het openbaar op straat hun geloof verkondigden, had Hij ongetwijfeld velen kunnen vinden die zo’n goed werk wilden doen. Maar God zal alleen degenen toestaan in de bres tussen Hem en de wereld te staan die het verdienen daar te zijn. Het is de universele trots van de mens die hem ertoe brengt te geloven dat hij alleen maar nuttig hoeft te willen zijn, waarna hij ook gebruikt zal worden. In Gods huis zijn er vaten tot eer en vaten tot oneer, maar een eervolle plaats verdienen is veel moeilijker dan er een te verlangen.

In onze tijd ontvangen we heel vaak post met de boodschap: ‘Krijg de erkenning die u verdient.’ Het is geen geheim dat de erkenning die velen verdienen nul is. Maar we zijn allemaal beïnvloed door de subliminale boodschap dat iedereen erkenning verdient. Onze samenleving propageert dat alle immorele, onbezonnen en onverstandige mensen dezelfde zorg verdienen als de morele en ijverige mensen. Als de luie persoon een goed loon verdient en de verkwister financiële zekerheid verdient, heeft de apostel Paulus beslist niet het recht om voorwaarden te stellen aan de weduwen die steun van de kerk behoren te ontvangen. Evenmin heeft hij het recht om een oprechte persoon die het ambt van opziener verlangt af te wijzen, alleen omdat die niet aan de vereisten voldoet. Maar God zag enkele mensen …in Sardis die hun kleren niet bevlekt hebben; zij zullen met Mij in het wit wandelen, want zij zijn het waard. –Openb 3:4.

Dit zijn mannen in de bres. Niet omdat ze over energie beschikten om te verbranden, maar omdat ze een visie op reinheid hadden. Dat was geen toeval, want mannen die bij God aanzien willen verwerven, moeten dat doen door middel van…

…Doel

Door het geloof weigerde Mozes, toen hij volwassen geworden was, een zoon van de dochter van Farao genoemd te worden. Hij verkoos liever met het volk van God slecht behandeld te worden dan tijdelijk van de zonde te genieten. Hij beschouwde de smaad van Christus als grotere rijkdom dan de schatten in Egypte, want hij had het oog gericht op de beloning. Door het geloof verliet hij Egypte zonder bevreesd te zijn voor de woede van de koning, want hij hield stand als zag hij de Onzichtbare. –Heb 11:24-27.

Een ware visie op Gods werk heeft een prijskaartje. De rijke jongeling had graag zowel heerser in het koninkrijk van Christus als heer op zijn landgoed willen zijn, maar hij kon niet beide zijn. Dit beginsel vormde de eerste hindernis voor hem en voor iedereen die zo’n edel werk zou willen doen. Als jonge man nam Mozes zijn besluit en koos hij partij. Hij was erop voorbereid door Egypte verworpen te worden, maar had nooit gedacht dat ook zijn eigen volk hem zo lichtvaardig zou afwijzen.

Veertig jaar in de eenzame smeltoven zuiverden zijn trots en snoeiden zijn kracht. Daar studeerde hij af aan het seminarie van de stilte, toegerust en voorbereid om als de zachtmoedigste man op aarde in de bres te staan. Hij werd een voorspreker voor mensen bij God. Als pleitbezorger voor mensen en voor God predikte en bad hij, wandelde en weende hij, leefde hij en had hij zijn God en zijn broeders lief. Dit alles terwijl hij zichzelf ongeschikt achtte voor de positie. Hoewel de kinderen van Israël hem na aan het hart lagen, verloren zijn vrees voor God en zijn aandacht voor Hem nooit hun plaats. Wanneer we door mensen gerespecteerd willen worden, raakt ons doel vertroebeld en geven we onze positie in de bres op. Veel goede predikanten, ouders en pelgrims hebben deze fout gemaakt en hun richtsnoer gekregen van hun vrouw, hun kinderen, hun vrienden of hun kerk. Misschien lijkt het liefdevol, zorgzaam en het meest respectvol om dat te doen. Maar God vereist absolute trouw en er kan geen compromis zijn. Wat een man ‘wil zijn’ wordt bepaald door zijn doelgerichte visie, maar wat hij ‘blijkt te zijn’ hangt af van zijn…

…Prioriteiten

Dit is een betrouwbaar woord: als iemand verlangen heeft naar het ambt van opziener, begeert hij een voortreffelijk werk. Een opziener moet dan onberispelijk zijn, de man van één vrouw, waakzaam, bezonnen, eerbaar, gastvrij, bekwaam om te onderwijzen; niet verslaafd aan wijn, niet opvliegend, niet uit op schandelijke winst, maar inschikkelijk, niet twistziek, niet geldzuchtig; iemand die zijn eigen huis goed bestuurt en zijn kinderen met alle waardigheid onderdanig houdt; –1 Tim 3:1-4. Ons doel bepaalt onze bestemming, maar onze prioriteiten banen de weg ernaartoe.

Helaas worden sommige mannen door de publieke opinie tot de bediening bevorderd, maar God kiest Zijn mannen op grond van hun prioriteiten en eeuwige vereisten. Mannen die door hun bezit, hartstochten of positie worden beheerst, zijn nutteloos voor Gods doel. Ze willen graag dominee, eerwaarde of vader worden genoemd. Ze willen graag worden beschouwd als ijverig, kundig, standvastig of meelevend. Zoek ik nu de gunst van mensen of die van God? Of probeer ik mensen te behagen? Als ik nog steeds mensen behaagde, zou ik geen dienaar van Christus zijn. –Gal 1:10 NBG.

Gelukkig is God geen aannemer des persoons, en een steen die geschikt is voor de muur zal niet aan de kant worden gelegd. Ouderen, armen, verminkten en kreupelen zijn allemaal uitstekende kandidaten om de bres te vullen. Mensen met gebroken dromen, gebroken lichamen en gebroken harten kunnen ongehinderd in de omheining naast Noach, Abraham, Jozef, Mozes, Daniël, Esther, Ruth en een ontelbaar legioen anderen staan. Zij zijn allemaal voortreffelijke vertegenwoordigers van God in deze wereld. Ze hebben allemaal de rug toegekeerd aan lichtzinnigheid, roem, vertrouwelijkheid en rijkdom, en zijn helden van de hemel geworden. Ze staan schouder aan schouder in de omheining en vormen de ‘Ambassade van de Eeuwige’. Zij hadden lief, terwijl anderen haatten. Zij gaven alles, terwijl anderen ontvingen. Er werd met hen gespot en ze werden verkeerd begrepen, beschimpt en bespot, vermoeid en huilend.

Want wij zijn voor God een aangename geur van Christus, onder hen die behouden worden en onder hen die verloren gaan. Voor de een zijn wij een geur van de dood die tot de dood leidt, voor de ander een geur van het leven die tot het leven leidt. En wie is tot deze dingen bekwaam? –2 Kor 2:15-16. Dat zijn zij wier enige doel en prioriteiten door God worden bepaald.
