«E busquei entre eles um homem que levantasse o muro e se pusesse na brecha diante de mim, em favor da terra, para que eu não a destruísse; mas não encontrei nenhum. –Ezequiel 22:30

A história do pequeno menino holandês que heroicamente enfiou o dedo no buraco do dique vem à mente quando consideramos um versículo como esse. Ele não podia sair dali, temendo a erosão, então passou a longa noite esperando, até que alguém apareceu pela manhã para livrá-lo de sua aflição. Muitos homens realizaram feitos extraordinários por impulso quando o momento assim exigiu. Vidas foram resgatadas, cidades foram salvas e inimigos foram derrotados porque alguém desempenhou um papel necessário. Livros são escritos e monumentos erguidos em honra daqueles cujo benefício nos tocou. Eles são considerados os heróis da história e são lembrados por sua firme coragem e fidelidade inabalável.

Mas as brechas da vida nem sempre são tão evidentes, e os resultados nem sempre são mensuráveis. Salomão nos relata a história de …uma pequena cidade, com poucos homens nela; e veio contra ela um grande rei, cercou-a e construiu grandes baluartes contra ela. Ora, havia nela um homem pobre e sábio, que por sua sabedoria livrou a cidade; contudo, ninguém se lembrou daquele homem pobre. –Ec 9:14-15. Embora a Bíblia nos ofereça muitas descrições detalhadas de homens piedosos que se puseram na brecha por Deus, sem dúvida há multidões de outros que venceram enormes desafios no plano espiritual e, ainda assim, não receberam reconhecimento nesta vida.

O problema não está tanto em que pôr-se na brecha esteja além de nossas capacidades ou recursos financeiros, mas no fato de que, muitas vezes, essa tarefa não tem título, ordenação nem reconhecimento. Ela deve ser realizada por voluntários com visão e dedicação suficientes para sacrificarem seus próprios planos pela única causa de tapar a brecha no muro. Muitas vezes, isso não pertence ao âmbito físico, mas aos limites do espiritual. Embora sempre tenhamos os pobres conosco, e a nobreza espiritual se disponha humildemente a ajudá-los, devemos considerar que provavelmente Deus tem em mente aqui algo além de precisar de alguém para organizar filas de distribuição de pão e refeitórios populares. Ele procura um homem vestido com um manto de «princípios púrpura» que não será despido quando as temperaturas subirem.

O rei Dario assinou o decreto fatídico destinado a levar Daniel a um almoço com os leões. Quando Daniel soube que o escrito estava assinado, entrou em sua casa e, com as janelas do seu quarto abertas na direção de Jerusalém, ajoelhou-se três vezes ao dia, orou e deu graças diante do seu Deus, como costumava fazer. –Dn 6:10. Que coisa insignificante teria sido Daniel fechar as persianas antes de orar! Mas Daniel não estava tapando a brecha apenas por sua presença no alto cargo governamental que ocupava. A brecha estava na escassez de testemunhas piedosas na Babilônia. Assim, a abertura entre o céu e a terra devia ser preenchida pela oração junto à janela aberta, enquanto ele sacrificava seu «assento no Senado».

A razão fundamental de existirem tantas brechas e tão poucos homens para tapá-las é que muitas vezes confundimos nossa visão pessoal e terrena das circunstâncias com os propósitos eternos de Deus. Estamos ocupados com coisas boas e nos sentimos bastante úteis. Marta agia com zelo para preencher aquilo que percebia como a necessidade iminente da casa, enquanto Maria estava sentada junto àquilo que era eterno. É incrivelmente fácil cair na armadilha da atividade de uma vida agitada. Podemos nos dedicar intensamente a subir com eficiência até o topo da escada, apenas para descobrir que ela está apoiada na parede errada. Muitas pessoas estão muito ocupadas, mas não são muito eficazes. Muitos trabalharam diligentemente durante anos na obra do Senhor, apenas para chegar à linha de chegada e perceber que as coisas mais importantes lhes escaparam. Alguns, ao dedicarem a vida ao serviço dos outros, deixaram o casamento sofrer ou permitiram que os filhos lhes faltassem ao respeito. Outros entregaram «Corbã» à sua igreja, negligenciando o relacionamento com os próprios pais.

O homem na brecha precisa ser sábio, e a sabedoria precisa compreender onde se encontra a verdadeira brecha. Nisso, devemos ser guiados por uma visão bíblica e determinada. A vida nos oferecerá muitas oportunidades para abandonarmos nosso rumo. Se buscarmos ativamente viver de acordo com as expectativas que nos são impostas por nossa família, nossos amigos, colegas, programas da igreja e circunstâncias da vida, seremos guiados por pessoas, e não por princípios bíblicos. Embora isso possa parecer legítimo à primeira vista, talvez colhamos a amarga decepção de nos vermos pendurados na ponta da corda errada.

Então, como é a brecha que preocupa a Deus? Alguns diriam que essa brecha aparece sempre que surge uma necessidade. Sempre temos os pobres conosco e, certamente, nisso há uma oportunidade de fazer o bem. Mas a melhor parte escolhida por Maria nada tinha a ver com ajudar os pobres ou alimentar os famintos. Da mesma forma, a mulher que possuía o precioso vaso de alabastro com perfume de nardo poderia tê-lo vendido e, com o valor obtido, sustentado os pobres por bastante tempo. Mas a brecha real não podia ser tapada acariciando o aleijado, mas coroando o Cristo. No Jardim do Éden não havia brecha, pois o homem vivia em perfeita harmonia com seu Criador. Foi o pecado que criou a brecha e perturbou o relacionamento. Também não haverá ruptura no fim dos tempos, quando o Cordeiro receber sua noiva. Até lá, há uma grande brecha, que existe porque esta terra se recusa a glorificar seu Criador. Pôr-se nessa brecha deve ser o propósito principal de todos os que aspiram a levar o nome dele.

Isso exige uma transformação completa em nosso relacionamento com Deus. A expiação pelo sangue de Cristo torna isso judicialmente possível. O consolo do Espírito Santo torna isso emocionalmente satisfatório, mas é no âmbito da nossa rendição e da glorificação de Deus que a cena ganha vida. O Filho Pródigo é um exemplo notável de uma alma que trouxe sobre si um mundo de problemas ao abandonar a posição que ocupava como filho de seu pai. Na base de sua restauração estava nada mais que o restabelecimento do relacionamento entre pai e filho que existia desde o seu nascimento.

Parece-me que Deus não está tanto à procura de almas que agitem as mãos no ar e gritem: «Eis-me aqui, envia-me!» Em vez disso, seus olhos procuram as almas humildes que submetem sua vontade diante do Todo-Poderoso e reconhecem: «Digno és, Senhor, de receber glória, honra e poder, porque criaste todas as coisas, e por tua vontade elas existem e foram criadas.» –Apocalipse 4:11. Não faltam filhos de Ceva que imaginam estar desempenhando um papel importante ao se disporem a anunciar o «Jesus» de quem ouviram falar. Em 1997, cerca de 800 mil homens chegaram a um encontro dos Promise Keepers em Washington, D.C., em resposta ao tema «Pôr-se na brecha». Esses homens talvez tivessem boas intenções ao representar Deus perante uma nação que se afastava rapidamente de seus fundamentos espirituais, mas é preciso mais do que um coração disposto. Deus não precisa de uma grande massa de corpos para enfiar numa brecha. Ele procura homens qualificados, e poucos foram promovidos a tal posição.

Se tudo o que Deus quisesse fosse que homens comparecessem a um encontro ou proclamassem publicamente sua fé nas ruas, sem dúvida poderia encontrar muitos desejosos de realizar uma boa obra desse tipo. Mas pôr-se na brecha entre Deus e o mundo só será autorizado por Deus para aqueles que merecem estar ali. É o orgulho universal do homem que o leva a acreditar que basta desejar ser útil para então ser usado. Na casa de Deus, há vasos para honra e vasos para desonra; no entanto, merecer um lugar honroso é muito mais difícil do que desejá-lo.

Em nossos dias, é muito comum receber correspondência com a mensagem: «Receba o reconhecimento que merece». Não é segredo que o reconhecimento que muitos merecem é nenhum. Mas todos fomos influenciados pela mensagem subliminar de que todos merecem reconhecimento. Nossa sociedade promove a ideia de que todas as pessoas imorais, imprudentes e imprevidentes merecem o mesmo cuidado que as pessoas morais e trabalhadoras. Se o indivíduo preguiçoso merece um bom salário e o gastador merece segurança financeira, então o apóstolo Paulo certamente não tem o direito de impor qualificações às viúvas que devem receber ajuda da igreja. Tampouco tem o direito de rejeitar qualquer alma sincera que deseje o cargo de bispo, apenas por não cumprir os requisitos. Mas Deus observou algumas almas …em Sardes que não contaminaram suas vestes; e andarão comigo vestidas de branco, pois são dignas. –Ap 3:4

Esses são homens na brecha. Não porque tivessem energia de sobra, mas porque tinham uma visão de pureza. Isso não foi mero acaso, pois os homens que desejam alcançar preeminência diante de Deus precisam fazê-lo por meio de…

…Propósito

Pela fé, Moisés, sendo já adulto, recusou ser chamado filho da filha de Faraó, escolhendo antes ser maltratado com o povo de Deus do que desfrutar por algum tempo os prazeres do pecado, considerando o opróbrio de Cristo riqueza maior do que os tesouros do Egito, pois tinha em vista a recompensa. Pela fé, abandonou o Egito, não temendo a ira do rei, pois perseverou como quem vê aquele que é invisível. –Hb 11:24-27

Uma verdadeira visão da obra de Deus virá com um preço. O jovem rico teria adorado ser governante no reino de Cristo e também em sua propriedade, mas não podia ficar com os dois. Esse princípio foi o primeiro obstáculo para ele e para todos os outros que desejariam uma obra tão nobre. Ainda jovem, Moisés tomou sua decisão e escolheu a quem seria leal. Estava preparado para ser rejeitado pelo Egito, mas jamais imaginou que seria também tão levianamente descartado pelo próprio povo.

Foram quarenta anos na fornalha solitária que purificaram seu orgulho e podaram sua capacidade. Ali, concluiu o seminário do silêncio, equipado e preparado para se pôr na brecha como o homem mais manso da face da terra. Tornou-se intercessor dos homens diante de Deus. Como defensor dos homens e de Deus, pregava e orava, caminhava e chorava, vivia e amava seu Deus e seus irmãos. Durante todo esse tempo, considerava-se inadequado para a posição. Embora os filhos de Israel estivessem no âmago de seu coração, seu temor e sua atenção nunca se afastaram de Deus. Quando procuramos ser respeitados pelos homens, nosso propósito fica obscurecido e perdemos nossa posição na brecha. Muitos bons pastores, pais e peregrinos cometeram esse erro e receberam suas orientações da esposa, dos filhos, dos amigos ou da igreja. Talvez pareça a atitude mais amorosa, atenciosa e respeitosa. Mas Deus exige fidelidade absoluta, e não pode haver concessões. Aquilo que um homem «quer ser» é determinado por seu propósito visionário, mas aquilo em que ele «acaba se tornando» depende de suas…

…Prioridades

Esta é uma palavra fiel: se alguém deseja o episcopado, deseja uma boa obra. É necessário, pois, que o bispo seja irrepreensível, marido de uma só mulher, vigilante, sóbrio, de bom comportamento, hospitaleiro, apto para ensinar; não dado ao vinho, não violento, não ávido de lucro desonesto, mas moderado, não briguento, não avarento; que governe bem a própria casa e mantenha os filhos em sujeição, com toda a dignidade; –1Tm 3:1-4. Nosso propósito determina nosso destino, mas são nossas prioridades que pavimentam o caminho até lá.

Infelizmente, alguns homens são promovidos ao ministério pela opinião popular, mas Deus escolhe seus homens com base em suas prioridades e qualificações eternas. Homens governados por suas posses, paixões ou posição serão inúteis para servir ao propósito de Deus. Gostam de ser chamados de Pastor, Reverendo ou Pai. Gostam de ser considerados zelosos, sábios, firmes ou compassivos. Porventura, procuro agora o favor dos homens ou o de Deus? Ou procuro agradar aos homens? Se ainda estivesse agradando aos homens, não seria servo de Cristo. –Gl 1:10 ASV

Felizmente, Deus não faz acepção de pessoas, e uma pedra adequada para o muro não será deixada de lado. Os idosos, os pobres, os mutilados e os coxos são todos candidatos ideais para preencher a brecha. Os que têm sonhos desfeitos, corpos feridos e corações partidos podem pôr-se sem impedimentos na brecha ao lado de Noé, Abraão, José, Moisés, Daniel, Ester, Rute e um incontável batalhão de outros. Todos eles são representantes notáveis de Deus para este mundo. Deram as costas à frivolidade, à fama, à familiaridade e à fortuna, e tornaram-se heróis do céu. Permanecem ombro a ombro na brecha e formam a «Embaixada do Eterno». Amaram enquanto outros odiaram. Deram tudo enquanto outros receberam. Foram escarnecidos e incompreendidos, insultados e ridicularizados, cansados e chorosos.

Porque somos para Deus o bom perfume de Cristo, entre os que se salvam e entre os que se perdem: para estes, cheiro de morte para morte; para aqueles, cheiro de vida para vida. E quem é suficiente para estas coisas? –2Co 2:15-16. São aqueles cujo único propósito e cujas prioridades são governados por Deus.

I have been told by many women folk here in Holmes County, Ohio, that we have excellent charity stores and second-hand shops, as is often the case where large groups of plain people are living. We have had people from all around come to visit, taking extra time to drop by these stores. Apparently, people here like to keep things in top shape, so at the first sign of wear, it’s “out with the old and in with the new.”

Likewise, no farmer would disagree that seeing all their machinery run like a top, and all their livestock stay healthy, is a satisfying feeling. Since the time of Adam, the Lord has always made us that way—to …have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth. –Gen 1:28

Having an opposite attitude is to be avoided. Jude exhorts us to beware of “certain men” who, within our midst, have “crept in unawares.” They live by the flesh and “despise dominion.” Two thousand years later, even in our overly casual society where “It’s all good” and we need to “Just chill,” the Lord still expects us to take seriously our calling to exercise God-given responsibility of dominion using Biblical principles in all that we do.

Does this dominion also extend to our own bodies? In Second Chronicles, Chapter 34, we can read of the wretched state of the Temple at the beginning of the reign of King Josiah, how he rebuilt it both physically with stone and timber—skillfully crafted by the artisans, and spiritually, by rediscovering and drinking in the Word of God. So too should we care for our bodies, as the Apostle Paul instructs us: What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own? For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God’s. –1Co 6:19-20

It is safe to say that judging by the multitude of nutritional supplements, chiropractors, doctors, and other various ancillary (supplemental) health care people and products, we make a good effort at keeping our physical temples well cared for and healthy. However, since we are all born with the curse of Adam, unlike machine parts that can simply be replaced, or a new machine purchased once the old one has run the full course of its life, we are faced with the reality that our body parts also have a practical “shelf life.” The older we get, the more apparent it is that life is very limited. The Bible says 70-80 years (–see Psa 90:10). (In America, in 2018, the average was 78.7 years. How little things have changed over 3 millennia later!)

I think we can all agree that God is primarily concerned about the spiritual temple, even more than the physical temple of our bodies. One doesn’t need to think hard to find godly men and women of today, and our spiritual forefathers of yesterday, who sacrificed and endured the destruction of their bodies, glorifying God, resulting in the cleansing of their souls and the future glorification of their bodies. Their plea was this: Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me. –Psa 51:10

Christ himself endured the destruction of His physical body, stating, …Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. –Joh 2:19. In the resurrection, his body was regenerated. We also read in scripture, about another physical regeneration, in which the earth will give birth to her dead; where those who dwell in the dust [will] wake up and shout for joy! (–see Isa 26:19)

Yet through this all, when our bodies break down or wear out, we feebly attempt, with some limited success, a physical regeneration of our own. There is a whole field of study focusing on Regenerative Medicine. The actual word “regeneration” literally means to “redo genesis” by recreating a new body—quite a lofty goal indeed!

Is there anything wrong with replacing broken parts (knees, hips and elbows), patching up broken pieces (bones and skin), and maintaining health in general (through good nutrition and physical activity)? Certainly not—it is how I make my living, advising and treating my patients! Yet like most things, even the pursuit of “good health” should give us pause to “count the costs” and exercise moderation—Let your moderation be known unto all men. The Lord is at hand. –Php 4:5. For while the pursuit of physical health is a good thing, it is a blind pursuit without regard to the spiritual costs (as we discovered in our series on vaccines), that can result in leading us astray and away from God.

There are two ditches on this road to physical health, spiritual health, and our overall well-being. In the ditch on the one hand, we can be reckless with our health, allowing our bodily temple to decay prematurely. Job said of man: Seeing his days are determined, the number of his months are with thee, thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass; –Job 14:5. So if we, through neglect, seek to cut those days short, are we not in defiance of God—seeking to short-circuit His perfect will for us? In the other ditch is the reckless and futile search for immortality—by seeking physical health at any cost. In doing so, is this not also an act of defiance? Paul reminds us: Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned: –Rom 5:12. In other words, due to sin, it is God’s plan for us to die physically (so that we may live eternally with Him).

Most readers, at this point would agree that both ends of the spectrum have this in common: they both neglect a person’s spiritual health, and they are both in a state of defiance toward God. So where am I going with this? Most Christians, who I know, do not pursue physical health at any cost. Bear with me then, as I would like to take the remainder of this article (and the next article) to give you a history of Regenerative Medicine—this “redoing of genesis.” Does it live up to its claims? Are there scams? What are the pitfalls? What does the future hold? Most importantly, how does it impact our spiritual health and our relationship with the Lord?

First, what exactly is Regenerative Medicine? As I mentioned previously, it literally means man’s efforts to “redo” genesis (origin, creation, or beginning). The term was first used as recently as the 1990s and is defined as the study and practice of “the replacement or regeneration of human cells, tissue, or organs, to restore or establish normal function.” In its short history, any and all means necessary to do this have been used.

It is different from Transplant Medicine in which whole organs are replaced but are still viewed as “foreign” by the receiving body. That is why strong anti-rejection medicines are needed for the rest of the individual’s life. It is also different from Orthopedic Medicine, in which hardware, such as screws, and titanium knees, for example, secure and replace warn out parts. Regenerative Medicine draws on the natural occurrence of certain organisms such as starfish, lizards, and lobsters, which are able to “regenerate” missing limbs and tails. In essence, the regenerated tissue is indistinguishable from the original, having few to no complications or side effects due to the fact that it is wholly integrated into that specific species’ host body. Sounds good doesn’t it?

This is not a new concept. Prometheus, in Greek mythology, was a “minor god,” who was punished by the “head god” Zeus (for “giving” fire to man) by having animals feast on his body, only to have his body regenerate the next day. A couple of thousand years later, Mary Shelly’s Frankenstein novel was subtitled “The Modern Prometheus.” This book, written almost exactly 200 years ago, contains a strong warning about unrestrained science, and man’s reckless search for fleshly regeneration. Even so, it is easy to see that man has had a long history of desire to regenerate his body, just as a mechanic swaps out parts or a starfish grows a new arm.

Advances in anesthesia, pharmacology (antibiotics and anti-rejection medicines in particular), surgery and sterilization techniques led to milestones in medicine, such as the first kidney transplant in 1954 and the first bone marrow transplant in 1968. But transplants had limitations—some injured and damaged tissues or complex organs, such as a brain, could not simply be replaced. Furthermore, due to an aging population and the sheer demands for the large quantities needed of some tissues, such as skin for burn victims, coupled with a chronic shortage of proper donors, alternatives were needed. Also, the dark shadow of tissue rejection was ever present and needed to be dealt with.

It has long been known that while an unborn child is a unique human being, it is rare for such developing children to be rejected by his or her mother’s body. We have learned this is due to the fact that in developing fetuses, their cells do not have many unique identifiers. The older a person becomes, the more their cells have a unique look and identification—kind of like the same fingerprint on the surface of each and every cell in a person’s body. A person’s body “knows” what its own tissue’s “fingerprint” looks like, and it “knows” that what isn’t native is foreign and must be attacked. By using fetal tissue, there would be almost no chance of rejection, and no need for dangerous life-long anti-rejection medicine. The new tissue would be entirely assimilated—so it was thought. So, attempts were made at using fetal tissue to cure things like Addison’s Disease (adrenal tissue) in the 1920s and Diabetes (pancreatic tissue) starting in the 1930s. While up to 24 fetuses were used per transplant, they eventually proved to be unsuccessful.1

By the 1990s, there was a renewed interest in using fetal tissue. Wouldn’t it be wonderful, some scientists thought, if, by simply inserting some fetal pancreatic insulin-producing cells under one’s forearms, diabetes could be cured? The same goes for fetal thyroid transplants, adrenal transplants—simply an outpatient procedure, and done in a few minutes. What about things like brain tissue for Parkinson’s disease or Alzheimer’s? The potential was seemingly limitless.

If that sounds somewhat macabre, there was an even more ominous side. It was shown experimentally in mice that one could successfully transplant fetal ovarian tissue.2 The idea was to transplant fetal ovarian tissue into infertile women (for example, survivors of childhood cancer in which the chemo rendered the girl infertile). This would sideline any “need” for IVF treatments. Imagine being a child born of a genetic mother that was aborted!

With the cultural abortion battles, there was an intense push to find a “cure.” Suppose there was a cure for Alzheimer’s or Diabetes? How many people would reject that cure if it came from fetal tissue? If they actually refused the treatment, how many of those people would voice their objection to abortion if a family member chose a curative (though unethical) treatment? If a parent of a diabetic child refused treatment, would it be considered child neglect, and would the state have grounds for forcibly treating the child or removing him or her from the home until treatment was received? In the end, one goal was that abortion would be justified in the minds of the population.

But something happened: The treatments didn’t work as planned in a significant number of patients. The treatments in a large number of Parkinson patients were actually described by the providing doctors as “catastrophic,” “absolutely devastating,” and “a real nightmare”.3 Instead of the classic muscle rigidity associated with Parkinson’s Disease, came jerking heads, flinging arms, and writhing bodies. The tissue did not “know” enough when to turn itself off, overproducing neurohormones, even forming tumors of skin, hair, and cartilage.4 Moreover, the tissue that “took” eventually died out by the same process that caused the Parkinson’s disease.5 The treatments were obviously stopped.

But at about this time, in the late 1990s, techniques were discovered that enabled researchers to isolate, and grow in great numbers, a certain cell called a “stem cell” from human embryos. Think of these rapidly growing stem cells as forming the stem of a plant. It is through them that the other types of cells are derived (leaves, flower, and fruit). These embryos, uniquely human, were obtained from “leftover” fertility treatments in which conception was initiated in a laboratory petri (glass) dish and allowed to grow to a cluster size. The desired cells were taken, and the rest destroyed. (In essence, these were “micro” abortions.)

Fetal tissue did not work as expected, partly because it was already too specialized and too “pre-programmed,” but also too impure, too costly, and too labor intensive—necessitating the harvesting of tissue from numerous aborted babies with a microscope and tweezers. Some scientists thought, why not obtain these stem cells, “program” them into the desired type of cell, and grow them to however many are needed?

In the next issue, I will tell you where the research currently stands, where there have been successes and failures, and how Christians can ethically navigate the turbulent waters of these times. It is amazing how the Lord opens doors, using the wonders of science, to create ethical alternatives for those who remain faithful to Him and His ways. It will be exciting to explain to you, how these “alternatives” have become the main focus of research and treatment for believers and unbelievers alike.

But before I leave you, I’d like to mention that over the years, I’ve had a number of people remark that these babies are being aborted anyway, so why not get some benefit from the tragedy, wouldn’t that be redemptive in a way?

Here is my (short list) of reasons why it would be unbiblical for Christians to benefit from unethical vaccines—and now fetal tissue treatments:

  1. The act of redemption cannot be separated from restitution and reconciliation. The very act of using fetal tissue only encourages further and expanded exploitation—just the opposite of restitution and reconciliation (where there needs to be a resolution to no longer repeat the sin). History has borne out that there is a multiplication of the sin, not the reduction. Where there was once one cell line, there are now dozens. Scientists are emboldened to do further, and even more unethical research, especially if there is no objection.

  2. The very word “redeem” means to purchase back something which was originally was yours, but now has become lost. The body of the unborn child was never ours to begin with, never ours to give, and never ours to profit from.

  3. Redemption always involves a sacrifice—of self. How can anyone sacrifice self by volunteering the body of another? (Heb 9:12) John 15:13 says, Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends. Some Christians are keen to use this verse to justify going to war. While there is definitely self-sacrifice in going to war, the goal is to make the enemy lay down THEIR lives. The utilitarian use of fetal tissue follows the same line of thinking, except that there is NO self-sacrifice in exploiting the body of an aborted baby.

  4. While Jesus’s redemption of mankind turned something horrid and ugly into something that glorifies God, it was an act of sanctification through holiness and righteousness. Regarding this issue, I can’t think of an act further removed from sanctification, holiness and righteousness—only opportunism. –see Psa 111:9 and 1 Co 1:30

  5. We cannot hope for the deliverance of God from evil—by participating in and benefiting from evil. We are forgiven our trespasses, only by forgiving, not by co-conspiring, only by repaying good for evil. –see Mat 5 & 6

  6. God finds the shedding of innocent blood abhorrent (He hates it!). –see Pro 6:17. We can only please God and can only receive atonement by purging ourselves from any association with this guilt—not by participating in it. –see Deu 21:8, 9. Can anyone imagine utilizing products such as soap and lamp shades made from holocaust victims who would have “died anyway”?

  7. When Saul destroyed the Amalekites, he kept the best of the loot—ostensibly as an offering to God (at least he said so when he was challenged by Samuel). –see 1 Sam 15 Why did God utterly reject His anointed king over this? Could it be that he did not want His chosen to profit or benefit from evil—even in the destruction of that evil? Could it be that by bringing the bounty of the wicked into the midst of his chosen people, His people risked becoming desensitized to that very same wickedness, and so became corrupted themselves? Samuel simultaneously wept and grieved over Saul, crying out to the Lord. If it is not us, then who will weep for us and for a fallen generation?

  8. The same could be said concerning the judgement of Achan’s secreted treasure following the defeat at Ai. In summary, if there is any personal benefit to be had following a tragedy or a judgement of another, the best way to tell if it is legitimate, is if the details are not cloaked in secrecy. (For the fruit of the Spirit is in all goodness and righteousness and truth;) Proving what is acceptable unto the Lord. And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather reprove them. –Eph 5:9-11

  9. There are alternatives—why lend justification to unethical practices? On the issue of pursuing alternative vaccines, it is a difficult process, but not impossible to do. Following Christ often times follows the more arduous path, rather than the path of least resistance. The example of our faithful forefathers bears this out.

Muchas mujeres de aquí, en el condado de Holmes, Ohio, me han dicho que tenemos excelentes tiendas benéficas y de segunda mano, como suele ocurrir donde viven grandes comunidades de gente sencilla. Ha venido gente de todas partes a visitarnos y se ha tomado el tiempo adicional para pasar por estas tiendas. Al parecer, aquí a la gente le gusta mantener las cosas en excelentes condiciones, así que, ante la primera señal de desgaste, «lo viejo afuera y lo nuevo adentro».

Del mismo modo, ningún agricultor estaría en desacuerdo con que ver toda su maquinaria funcionar a la perfección y todo su ganado mantenerse sano es una sensación satisfactoria. Desde los tiempos de Adán, el Señor siempre nos ha hecho así: …señoread en los peces del mar, en las aves de los cielos y en todo ser viviente que se mueve sobre la tierra. –Gén 1:28

Hay que evitar una actitud opuesta. Judas nos exhorta a cuidarnos de «ciertos hombres» que, en medio de nosotros, «se han infiltrado encubiertamente». Viven según la carne y «desprecian la autoridad». Dos mil años después, incluso en nuestra sociedad excesivamente despreocupada, donde «todo está bien» y necesitamos «simplemente relajarnos», el Señor sigue esperando que nos tomemos en serio nuestro llamado a ejercer la responsabilidad de dominio que Dios nos ha dado, usando principios bíblicos en todo lo que hacemos.

¿Se extiende también este dominio a nuestro propio cuerpo? En Segundo de Crónicas, capítulo 34, podemos leer sobre el deplorable estado del Templo al comienzo del reinado del rey Josías, y cómo lo reconstruyó tanto físicamente, con piedra y madera —trabajadas hábilmente por los artesanos— como espiritualmente, al redescubrir y asimilar la Palabra de Dios. Así también debemos cuidar nuestros cuerpos, como nos instruye el apóstol Pablo: ¿No sabéis que vuestro cuerpo es templo del Espíritu Santo, que está en vosotros, el cual tenéis de Dios, y que no sois vuestros? Porque habéis sido comprados por precio; glorificad, pues, a Dios en vuestro cuerpo y en vuestro espíritu, los cuales son de Dios. –1 Co 6:19-20

Es razonable decir que, a juzgar por la multitud de suplementos nutricionales, quiroprácticos, médicos y otros diversos profesionales y productos complementarios de atención médica, hacemos un buen esfuerzo por mantener nuestros templos físicos bien cuidados y sanos. Sin embargo, dado que todos nacemos bajo la maldición de Adán, a diferencia de las piezas de una máquina, que simplemente pueden reemplazarse, o de una máquina nueva que puede comprarse cuando la vieja ha cumplido su vida útil, nos enfrentamos a la realidad de que las partes de nuestro cuerpo también tienen una «vida útil» práctica. Cuanto mayores nos hacemos, más evidente resulta que la vida es muy limitada. La Biblia dice que son 70-80 años (–véase Sal 90:10). (En Estados Unidos, en 2018, el promedio fue de 78,7 años. ¡Qué poco han cambiado las cosas más de tres milenios después!)

Creo que todos podemos estar de acuerdo en que a Dios le preocupa principalmente el templo espiritual, incluso más que el templo físico de nuestro cuerpo. No hace falta pensar mucho para encontrar hombres y mujeres piadosos de hoy, y nuestros antepasados espirituales de ayer, que sacrificaron y soportaron la destrucción de sus cuerpos, glorificando a Dios, lo que resultó en la purificación de sus almas y la futura glorificación de sus cuerpos. Esta era su súplica: Crea en mí, oh Dios, un corazón limpio, y renueva un espíritu recto dentro de mí. –Sal 51:10

Cristo mismo soportó la destrucción de su cuerpo físico, diciendo: …Destruid este templo, y en tres días lo levantaré. –Jn 2:19. En la resurrección, su cuerpo fue regenerado. También leemos en las Escrituras acerca de otra regeneración física, cuando la tierra dará a luz a sus muertos; cuando quienes habitan en el polvo [despierten] y griten de alegría. (–véase Is 26:19)

Sin embargo, a través de todo esto, cuando nuestros cuerpos se deterioran o desgastan, intentamos débilmente, con cierto éxito limitado, una regeneración física por cuenta propia. Existe todo un campo de estudio dedicado a la Medicina regenerativa. La palabra «regeneración» significa literalmente «rehacer la génesis», recreando un cuerpo nuevo: ¡un objetivo ciertamente muy ambicioso!

¿Hay algo de malo en reemplazar partes rotas (rodillas, caderas y codos), reparar partes dañadas (huesos y piel) y mantener la salud en general (mediante una buena nutrición y actividad física)? Por supuesto que no: ¡así me gano la vida, asesorando y tratando a mis pacientes! Sin embargo, como ocurre con la mayoría de las cosas, incluso la búsqueda de la «buena salud» debería hacernos detenernos a «calcular el costo» y ejercer moderación: Vuestra moderación sea conocida de todos los hombres. El Señor está cerca. –Fil 4:5. Porque, aunque buscar la salud física es algo bueno, hacerlo ciegamente, sin tener en cuenta los costos espirituales (como descubrimos en nuestra serie sobre las vacunas), puede desviarnos y alejarnos de Dios.

Hay dos zanjas en este camino hacia la salud física, la salud espiritual y nuestro bienestar general. En la zanja de un lado, podemos ser imprudentes con nuestra salud y permitir que el templo de nuestro cuerpo se deteriore prematuramente. Job dijo acerca del hombre: Puesto que sus días están determinados, y el número de sus meses está contigo, tú le has fijado sus límites, que no puede traspasar; –Job 14:5. Así que, si por descuido procuramos acortar esos días, ¿no estamos desafiando a Dios, tratando de frustrar su voluntad perfecta para nosotros? En la otra zanja está la búsqueda imprudente e inútil de la inmortalidad, procurando la salud física a cualquier costo. Al hacerlo, ¿no es también esto un acto de desafío? Pablo nos recuerda: Por tanto, como el pecado entró en el mundo por un hombre, y por el pecado la muerte, así la muerte pasó a todos los hombres, por cuanto todos pecaron: –Rom 5:12. En otras palabras, debido al pecado, el plan de Dios para nosotros es que muramos físicamente (para que podamos vivir eternamente con Él).

La mayoría de los lectores, llegados a este punto, estaría de acuerdo en que ambos extremos tienen algo en común: ambos descuidan la salud espiritual de la persona y ambos están en un estado de desafío a Dios. Entonces, ¿adónde quiero llegar con esto? La mayoría de los cristianos que conozco no buscan la salud física a cualquier costo. Les pido que me acompañen, pues quisiera dedicar el resto de este artículo (y el siguiente) a contarles la historia de la Medicina regenerativa, esta «recreación de la génesis». ¿Está a la altura de sus afirmaciones? ¿Hay estafas? ¿Cuáles son los riesgos? ¿Qué depara el futuro? Y, lo más importante, ¿qué impacto tiene en nuestra salud espiritual y en nuestra relación con el Señor?

Primero, ¿qué es exactamente la Medicina regenerativa? Como mencioné antes, significa literalmente los esfuerzos del hombre por «rehacer» la génesis (origen, creación o comienzo). El término se usó por primera vez hace apenas unas décadas, en los años noventa, y se define como el estudio y la práctica del «reemplazo o regeneración de células, tejidos u órganos humanos para restaurar o establecer su función normal». En su breve historia, se han utilizado todos los medios necesarios para lograrlo.

Es diferente de la Medicina de trasplantes, en la que se reemplazan órganos enteros, pero el cuerpo receptor sigue considerándolos «extraños». Por eso se necesitan medicamentos potentes contra el rechazo durante el resto de la vida de la persona. También es diferente de la Medicina ortopédica, en la que elementos como tornillos y rodillas de titanio, por ejemplo, fijan y reemplazan las partes desgastadas. La Medicina regenerativa se inspira en la capacidad natural de ciertos organismos, como las estrellas de mar, los lagartos y las langostas, que pueden «regenerar» extremidades y colas perdidas. En esencia, el tejido regenerado es indistinguible del original y presenta pocas complicaciones o efectos secundarios, o ninguno, porque se integra por completo en el cuerpo huésped de esa especie. Suena bien, ¿no?

No es un concepto nuevo. En la mitología griega, Prometeo era un «dios menor» a quien el «dios principal», Zeus, castigó (por «dar» el fuego al hombre) haciendo que los animales devoraran su cuerpo, que volvía a regenerarse al día siguiente. Unos dos mil años después, la novela de Mary Shelly, Frankenstein, llevaba como subtítulo «El moderno Prometeo». Este libro, escrito hace casi exactamente 200 años, contiene una severa advertencia contra la ciencia sin restricciones y la búsqueda imprudente del hombre de regenerar la carne. Aun así, es fácil ver que el hombre ha deseado durante mucho tiempo regenerar su cuerpo, tal como un mecánico cambia piezas o una estrella de mar hace crecer un brazo nuevo.

Los avances en anestesia, farmacología (en particular, los antibióticos y los medicamentos contra el rechazo), cirugía y técnicas de esterilización dieron lugar a hitos en la medicina, como el primer trasplante de riñón en 1954 y el primer trasplante de médula ósea en 1968. Pero los trasplantes tenían limitaciones: algunos tejidos lesionados o dañados, o algunos órganos complejos, como el cerebro, no podían simplemente reemplazarse. Además, debido al envejecimiento de la población y a la enorme demanda de las grandes cantidades necesarias de algunos tejidos, como la piel para las víctimas de quemaduras, sumada a la escasez crónica de donantes adecuados, hacían falta alternativas. También estaba siempre presente la oscura amenaza del rechazo de tejidos, que era necesario afrontar.

Desde hace mucho se sabe que, aunque el niño no nacido es un ser humano único, es poco común que el cuerpo de su madre rechace a esos niños en desarrollo. Hemos aprendido que esto se debe a que las células de los fetos en desarrollo no tienen muchos identificadores únicos. A medida que una persona envejece, sus células adquieren un aspecto y una identificación más singulares, algo parecido a que cada célula del cuerpo de una persona tuviera la misma huella dactilar en su superficie. El cuerpo de una persona «sabe» cómo es la «huella dactilar» de sus propios tejidos y «sabe» que lo que no es propio es extraño y debe ser atacado. Al utilizar tejido fetal, casi no habría posibilidad de rechazo ni necesidad de medicamentos peligrosos contra el rechazo durante toda la vida. Se pensaba que el tejido nuevo se asimilaría por completo. Así que se hicieron intentos de usar tejido fetal para curar enfermedades como la enfermedad de Addison (tejido suprarrenal) en los años veinte y la diabetes (tejido pancreático) a partir de los años treinta. Aunque se utilizaron hasta 24 fetos por trasplante, finalmente se demostró que los intentos fracasaban.1

Para los años noventa, volvió a aumentar el interés por el uso de tejido fetal. ¿No sería maravilloso, pensaron algunos científicos, si la diabetes pudiera curarse con solo insertar bajo los antebrazos unas células fetales productoras de insulina del páncreas? Lo mismo se pensó de los trasplantes fetales de tiroides y de glándulas suprarrenales: un sencillo procedimiento ambulatorio, realizado en unos minutos. ¿Y qué decir de tejidos cerebrales para la enfermedad de Parkinson o el alzhéimer? Las posibilidades parecían ilimitadas.

Si eso suena algo macabro, había un aspecto aún más siniestro. En experimentos con ratones se demostró que era posible trasplantar con éxito tejido ovárico fetal.2 La idea era trasplantar tejido ovárico fetal a mujeres infértiles (por ejemplo, sobrevivientes de cáncer infantil cuya quimioterapia las había dejado infértiles). Así se prescindiría de cualquier «necesidad» de tratamientos de fecundación in vitro. ¡Imaginen ser un niño nacido de una madre genética que fue abortada!

En medio de las batallas culturales en torno al aborto, se hizo un intenso esfuerzo por encontrar una «cura». ¿Y si hubiera una cura para el alzhéimer o la diabetes? ¿Cuántas personas rechazarían esa cura si procediera de tejido fetal? Si realmente rechazaran el tratamiento, ¿cuántas de esas personas expresarían su oposición al aborto si un familiar eligiera un tratamiento curativo (aunque poco ético)? Si un padre se negara a tratar a un hijo diabético, ¿se consideraría negligencia infantil? ¿Tendría el Estado motivos para obligar a tratar al niño o separarlo de su hogar hasta que recibiera tratamiento? En última instancia, uno de los objetivos era que el aborto quedara justificado en la opinión pública.

Pero ocurrió algo: los tratamientos no funcionaron como se esperaba en un número considerable de pacientes. Los médicos que los administraron describieron los tratamientos de un gran número de pacientes con párkinson como «catastróficos», «absolutamente devastadores» y «una verdadera pesadilla».3 En lugar de la rigidez muscular típica asociada con la enfermedad de Parkinson, aparecieron cabezas que se sacudían, brazos que se agitaban y cuerpos que se retorcían. El tejido no «sabía» cuándo debía dejar de activarse; producía un exceso de neurohormonas e incluso formaba tumores de piel, pelo y cartílago.4 Además, el tejido que «prendía» acababa muriendo por el mismo proceso que causaba la enfermedad de Parkinson.5 Evidentemente, se suspendieron los tratamientos.

Pero por esa época, a finales de los años noventa, se descubrieron técnicas que permitían a los investigadores aislar y cultivar en grandes cantidades un tipo de célula llamado «célula madre» a partir de embriones humanos. Piensen en estas células madre de rápido crecimiento como si formaran el tallo de una planta. De ellas se derivan los demás tipos de células (hojas, flores y frutos). Estos embriones, que son seres humanos, se obtenían de tratamientos de fertilidad «sobrantes», en los que la concepción se iniciaba en una placa de Petri (de vidrio) en un laboratorio y se dejaba crecer hasta formar un grupo de células. Se extraían las células deseadas y se destruía el resto. (En esencia, eran abortos «micro».)

El tejido fetal no funcionó como se esperaba, en parte porque ya estaba demasiado especializado y «preprogramado», pero también porque era demasiado impuro, costoso y laborioso, pues era necesario recolectar tejido de numerosos bebés abortados con un microscopio y pinzas. Algunos científicos pensaron: ¿por qué no obtener estas células madre, «programarlas» para que se conviertan en el tipo de célula deseado y cultivarlas en la cantidad que se necesite?

En el próximo número les contaré en qué punto se encuentra actualmente la investigación, dónde ha habido éxitos y fracasos, y cómo los cristianos pueden navegar éticamente las turbulentas aguas de estos tiempos. Es asombroso cómo el Señor abre puertas y utiliza las maravillas de la ciencia para crear alternativas éticas para quienes permanecen fieles a Él y a sus caminos. Será emocionante explicarles cómo estas «alternativas» se han convertido en el principal foco de investigación y tratamiento, tanto para creyentes como para no creyentes.

Pero antes de despedirme, quisiera mencionar que a lo largo de los años varias personas me han comentado que, de todos modos, esos bebés van a ser abortados, así que ¿por qué no obtener algún beneficio de la tragedia? ¿No sería eso redentor de alguna manera?

Esta es mi (breve lista de) razones por las que sería antibíblico que los cristianos se beneficiaran de vacunas poco éticas y, ahora, de tratamientos con tejido fetal:

  1. El acto de redención no puede separarse de la restitución y la reconciliación. El acto mismo de usar tejido fetal solo fomenta una explotación mayor y más extendida: justamente lo contrario de la restitución y la reconciliación (que requieren resolver no volver a repetir el pecado). La historia ha demostrado que el pecado se multiplica, no se reduce. Donde antes había una línea celular, ahora hay docenas. Los científicos se envalentonan para realizar investigaciones aún más poco éticas, especialmente si nadie objeta.

  2. La palabra «redimir» significa comprar de vuelta algo que originalmente era tuyo, pero que se perdió. El cuerpo del niño no nacido nunca fue nuestro, nunca nos correspondió entregarlo y nunca nos correspondió obtener ganancias de él.

  3. La redención siempre implica un sacrificio: el de uno mismo. ¿Cómo puede alguien sacrificarse ofreciendo el cuerpo de otra persona? (Heb 9:12) Juan 15:13 dice: Nadie tiene mayor amor que este, que uno ponga su vida por sus amigos. Algunos cristianos se apresuran a usar este versículo para justificar ir a la guerra. Aunque ir a la guerra implica ciertamente sacrificio propio, el objetivo es hacer que el enemigo entregue SU vida. El uso utilitario de tejido fetal sigue la misma lógica, salvo que NO hay sacrificio propio en explotar el cuerpo de un bebé abortado.

  4. Aunque la redención de la humanidad por Jesús convirtió algo horrible y repugnante en algo que glorifica a Dios, fue un acto de santificación por medio de la santidad y la justicia. En cuanto a este asunto, no se me ocurre ningún acto más alejado de la santificación, la santidad y la justicia: solo oportunismo. –véase Sal 111:9 e 1 Co 1:30

  5. No podemos esperar que Dios nos libre del mal participando en él y beneficiándonos de él. Nuestros pecados nos son perdonados solo si perdonamos, no si conspiramos con otros; solo si devolvemos bien por mal. –véase Mat 5 y 6

  6. Dios aborrece el derramamiento de sangre inocente (¡lo odia!). –véase Prov 6:17. Solo podemos agradar a Dios y recibir expiación si nos purificamos de toda asociación con esta culpa, no participando en ella. –véase Deut 21:8, 9. ¿Puede alguien imaginarse usando productos como jabón y pantallas de lámparas hechos con las víctimas del Holocausto, que «de todos modos habrían muerto»?

  7. Cuando Saúl destruyó a los amalecitas, se quedó con lo mejor del botín, supuestamente como ofrenda a Dios (al menos eso dijo cuando Samuel lo confrontó). –véase 1 Sam 15. ¿Por qué rechazó Dios por completo a su rey ungido por esto? ¿Será que no quería que sus elegidos obtuvieran ganancias o beneficios del mal, ni siquiera al destruirlo? ¿Será que, al introducir el botín de los malvados entre su pueblo elegido, su pueblo corría el riesgo de insensibilizarse ante esa misma maldad y, así, corromperse? Samuel lloró y se lamentó al mismo tiempo por Saúl, clamando al Señor. Si no nosotros, ¿quién llorará por nosotros y por una generación caída?

  8. Lo mismo podría decirse del juicio sobre el tesoro que Acán había escondido después de la derrota en Hai. En resumen, si se obtiene algún beneficio personal tras una tragedia o el juicio de otra persona, la mejor manera de saber si es legítimo es comprobar si los detalles están ocultos en secreto. (Porque el fruto del Espíritu consiste en toda bondad, justicia y verdad;) comprobando lo que agrada al Señor. Y no participéis en las obras infructuosas de las tinieblas; antes bien, reprendedlas. –Ef 5:9-11

  9. Hay alternativas: ¿por qué dar justificación a prácticas poco éticas? En cuanto a buscar vacunas alternativas, es un proceso difícil, pero no imposible. Seguir a Cristo muchas veces implica tomar el camino más arduo, en lugar del camino de menor resistencia. El ejemplo de nuestros fieles antepasados lo demuestra.

Notas finales:

The cold, grey days of winter are being transformed into the warm, sunny days of spring. The first flowers of the year are persistently pushing their way up out of the cold earth towards the warmth of the sun. It never seems to get old—this exciting feeling in the springtime air. There’s the warmth and light of sunny days. There’s the cheery, lilting music of the song birds as they once more take up housekeeping with seemingly boundless energy. And we are again blessed with another season to plant seeds with the expectation of another crop of food to enjoy.

This year I will turn 48 years of age. My how that sounds old to me. I remember that as a youth I thought that folks who were 50 were old. Now I am almost there. For me, this is a clear reminder that we all are getting older and that we will not live forever. Next, comes a number of sobering thoughts: “What have I done for the furtherance of God’s Kingdom? Am I remaining faithful to Him in all that I do? Lord, what wilt thou have me to do—this year?” Let’s, each one, prayerfully seek the Lord about His present and future will for our lives. Let’s encourage and exhort each other to remain faithful in relationship with, and in service for, our Master.

We feel that this marriage article is quite thorough in its evaluation of building and maintaining a Biblical foundation. Lord willing, we plan to have ongoing articles relating to this subject.

सर्दियों के ठंडे, धूसर दिन वसंत के गर्म, धूपभरे दिनों में बदल रहे हैं। साल के पहले फूल ठंडी मिट्टी से बाहर निकलकर सूर्य की गर्माहट की ओर लगातार बढ़ रहे हैं। वसंत की हवा में उमंग का यह एहसास कभी पुराना नहीं पड़ता। धूपभरे दिनों की गर्माहट और रोशनी है। गीत गाने वाले पक्षियों का उल्लासभरा, लयात्मक संगीत है, जब वे एक बार फिर मानो असीम ऊर्जा के साथ अपना बसेरा बसाते हैं। और हमें फिर से एक और मौसम का आशीर्वाद मिला है, जिसमें हम इस आशा से बीज बो सकते हैं कि खाने के लिए एक और फसल मिलेगी।

इस वर्ष मैं 48 वर्ष का हो जाऊँगा। अरे, यह सुनने में मुझे कितना बूढ़ा लगता है। मुझे याद है कि युवावस्था में मैं सोचता था कि 50 वर्ष के लोग बूढ़े होते हैं। अब मैं उस उम्र के लगभग करीब हूँ। मेरे लिए यह स्पष्ट याद दिलाता है कि हम सब बूढ़े हो रहे हैं और हमेशा जीवित नहीं रहेंगे। इसके बाद कई गंभीर विचार आते हैं: “मैंने परमेश्वर के राज्य की उन्नति के लिए क्या किया है? क्या मैं अपने हर काम में उसके प्रति विश्वासयोग्य बना हुआ हूँ? प्रभु, इस वर्ष तू मुझसे क्या करवाना चाहता है?” आइए, हम में से हर कोई प्रार्थनापूर्वक अपने जीवन के लिए प्रभु की वर्तमान और भावी इच्छा के विषय में उसकी खोज करे। आइए, एक-दूसरे को अपने स्वामी के साथ संबंध में और उसकी सेवा में विश्वासयोग्य बने रहने के लिए प्रोत्साहित करें और आग्रह करें।

इस अंक में विवाह पर एक उत्कृष्ट लेख है, जिसे हमने सोचा कि इस बार शिष्यत्व पर लेख के स्थान पर रखा जा सकता है। जब हम ऐसे दंपतियों से मिलते हैं जो वर्षों से विवाह की गंभीर समस्याओं से जूझ रहे हैं, तो हम आम तौर पर पाते हैं कि बुनियादी स्तर पर कुछ ईश्वरीय रीति से काम नहीं कर रहा है। हमें लगता है कि विवाह पर यह लेख बाइबिल के आधार को बनाने और बनाए रखने का काफी व्यापक मूल्यांकन करता है। प्रभु की इच्छा हुई तो हम इस विषय से संबंधित लेख आगे भी प्रकाशित करने की योजना रखते हैं।

इस आने वाले जुलाई में पेंसिल्वेनिया के लेबनान काउंटी में बैठकों की एक श्रृंखला में भाग लेने का हमारा कार्यक्रम है। उस क्षेत्र के कई चर्च इस आयोजन को संभव बनाने के लिए मिलकर काम कर रहे हैं और उन्होंने Fairview Reception Center आरक्षित किया है। कृपया इन बैठकों के लिए प्रार्थना करें: कि परमेश्वर की इच्छा पूरी हो; कि परमेश्वर वक्ताओं को तैयारी करते समय मार्गदर्शन दे; और कि इस प्रयास के माध्यम से परमेश्वर कलीसिया को सामर्थ्य दे। कृपया यह जानकारी उन लोगों तक पहुँचाएँ जिनकी इसमें रुचि हो सकती है। साथ ही, तारीख सुरक्षित रखने के लिए अपने कैलेंडर में इसे दर्ज कर लें।

यदि सभी विवरण अंतिम रूप दिए जाने के बाद आप अद्यतन जानकारी पाना चाहते हैं, तो कृपया “The Berean Voice” से फोन पर (330) 439-9547 या ईमेल द्वारा subscribe@bereanvoice.org पर संपर्क करें। भोजन की व्यवस्था और बैठने की सीमित जगह के कारण, इस आयोजन के लिए पंजीकरण आवश्यक होगा। नीचे इस श्रृंखला और संदेशों के अस्थायी शीर्षक दिए गए हैं, लेकिन उनमें अभी बदलाव हो सकता है।

“मानसिक, भावनात्मक, वैवाहिक और यौन दुर्व्यवहार संबंधी समस्याओं पर बाइबिल का दृष्टिकोण”

  1. हृदय को समझना—सभी समस्याओं की जड़
  2. सुसमाचार—मनुष्य की आत्मा और मन (psyche) से जुड़ी सभी समस्याओं के लिए परमेश्वर का उत्तर
  3. आज मनोविज्ञान और सांसारिक दर्शन हमें कैसे प्रभावित करते हैं
  4. व्यावहारिक शिष्यत्व—लोगों को बदलने में प्रभावी ढंग से सहायता करना
  5. मानसिक विकारों पर बाइबिल का दृष्टिकोण
  6. गोद लेने और पालन-पोषण से जुड़े मुद्दों का बाइबिल के अनुसार मूल्यांकन
  7. प्लेसिबो प्रभाव को समझना और मन को प्रभावित करने वाली दवाओं का सुरक्षित उपयोग
  8. नैतिक चूक, अश्लील सामग्री और यौन दुर्व्यवहार की बाइबिल के अनुसार समझ (केवल वयस्कों के लिए)
  9. पवित्रता—जन्म से लेकर मन-फिराव तक, फिर विवाह या अविवाहित जीवन तक (केवल माता-पिताओं के लिए)
  10. ईश्वरीय घरों के माध्यम से समस्याओं को रोकना और उनका समाधान करना
  11. स्थानीय कलीसिया के भीतर जीवन के सभी संघर्षों को रोकना और उनमें सहायता करना

Before I was converted, I had never heard the term “Anabaptist” and the concept of someone sharing their faith in Jesus with others was foreign to me. After I was converted, I remember thinking about all my friends who didn’t know anything about what had just happened to me. One thing kept going through my mind, “I need to tell them!” When something good happens to someone, they usually tell others. Some people tell one or two, while others feel like telling everyone. That’s what I wanted to do, not for my sake, but for theirs.

Whenever I would see an old friend, I would tell them what had happened to me. They usually said they had heard about it and then tried to get me to settle down and relax. I will be the first to admit, I made mistakes those first years. I noticed that many people didn’t appreciate what I had to say, but what astonished me the most was that the people who claimed to be Christians seemed to be the most offended.

One day I was visiting with an older man who said that he had been a Christian for most his life. During the discussion he pointed up to a lightbulb and said “Do you see that lightbulb? It’s not speaking.” I was shocked. He was telling me that, yes, Jesus says we are the light of the world, but that lights are quiet. They don’t speak. I went home to do a personal Bible study on the matter. Was this true? It wasn’t long before I found verses like, And Jesus went about all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing all manner of sickness and all manner of disease among the people. –Mat 4:23. Also, in Matthew, Jesus says that He was moved with compassion because the people with Him were tired and scattered about. Further on, we read, Then saith he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few; Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest. –Mat 9:37-38

It seems to me that wherever Jesus went, He was talking to people about the kingdom. I have seen people witnessing about God but doing it in an ugly way. That doesn’t mean we shouldn’t witness. If you read the book of Acts, that’s about all you see—believers sharing the Gospel message with others! In one account the authorities captured the disciples and said they could go free if they would be quiet! The disciples, though, said they could not—For we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard. –Act 4:20. Eventually, they were permanently silenced—by death.

I later heard about these people called Anabaptists. I began to read about them, and how they, too would not be silent. I ordered the Martyr’s Mirror and was astounded at what I read. These dear people lived like the disciples that we find in the Bible. They fulfilled the things Jesus said,—And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved. –Mat 10:22. And in Romans, As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter. –Rom 8:36. After some time, I found a church with an Anabaptist vision.

So why am I writing this? Dear brothers and sisters, I believe the fire is going out. I keep hearing some of our Anabaptist people talking about living a quiet and peaceable life. Jesus tells us in the parable of the sower, He also that received seed among the thorns is he that heareth the word; and the care of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, choke the word, and he becometh unfruitful. –Mat 13:22. Could that be where some of us are at? We live in a western culture where money seems easy to obtain, and we become focused on our own wealth and the cares of this world. Let’s be careful that we don’t become like the world, to avoid being persecuted by the world.

One group of Anabaptists was fleeing persecution and moved into a country not yet persecuted. They began a furniture shop to support themselves, but they couldn’t sell any furniture because they were the dreaded Anabaptists. Soon the situation got desperate because they needed money for food. One day a wealthy man walked into the shop. All the workers stopped working. “Maybe this man will buy something, and we can eat!” They thought. An old brother approached the possible client and asked him if he knew Jesus. After a short chat the man stormed out of the store in a fit of anger. Soon some hungry workers asked the old man why he had to scare away their only chance at a sale. He explained that for this man to know Jesus was far more important than them worrying about making a sale. That was the mindset of the early Anabaptists—the Gospel was number one. They couldn’t but speak of the things they’d seen and heard and they, too, were killed all the day long.

I’ve read numerous accounts of early Anabaptist Christians who had been arrested for their faith. The authorities would plead with them to just be quiet! But they refused, just as the disciples did. They too chose death, rather than the quiet life. One young man was arrested that left behind his dear wife expecting their first child. The authorities waited for the child to be born then brought the newborn infant to the new father in prison. They told him he was now a father and could go home and be with his wife and son. They said he could also continue to believe the same way, but he had to keep quiet, and not speak out against sin in the church. The young father refused, so they burnt him at the stake. Being quiet was not an option.

So, what do the Scriptures mean about a quiet and peaceable life? Paul writes to Timothy, I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men; For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty. –1Ti 2:1-2. For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty? Yes, the apostle Paul says this, but what did he mean? Could he have meant that we should be quiet about the Gospel? Or that we should never confront a sinner? Paul is not telling us to do something that he never did, or something that Christ himself never did. In fact, the Scriptures, reveal something quite the opposite.

It seems that the New Testament Christians in the Bible and in the early church were actively spreading the Gospel and were excited about the Church of Jesus Christ. They went about preaching the Gospel: holding meetings in the mountains, in the woods, or anywhere people would come. That was their life. Paul here is saying that we should pray that if we are obeying God by doing things the authorities don’t like, that they will leave us alone as we go about our normal day-to-day activities. As Christians, we should be spreading the truth of God’s Word, and being active for the furtherance of God’s Kingdom. Our prayer should be that the authorities will let us live in peace, while serving the Prince of Peace.

Some Christians try to be the world in their efforts to win the world. Trying to get people to live a happy life, join our club, be free in Christ, go on an exciting mission trip, live life to the fullest, be everything you can be. It’s all about “loving Jesus,” not obeying Him.

What about us? Are we excited to tell people about Jesus even if it will cost us something? For many of us it is quite easy to talk about farming, construction work, deer hunting, and many other things, yet when it comes to the things of God, we don’t have much to say. Are we that scared of persecution? Do we fear the world hating us? Remember what Jesus said, If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you. If ye were of the world, the world would love his own… –Joh 15:18-19. And, Whosoever therefore shall be ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation; of him also shall the Son of man be ashamed, when he cometh in the glory of his Father with the holy angels. –Mar 8:38

It’s easy to be a Christian, where you settle down and live a quiet and peaceable life, never challenging a sinner, never correcting a brother, or never stepping on Satan’s toes, but who said it would be easy? Here in Haiti we, as a church, are trying to follow Jesus no matter what the cost. Just yesterday we had two members tell us they are about to lose their jobs because of the Gospel. Another sister in the church reported that the school where her children attend require uniforms and that the girls must wear pants. She sent her daughter to school in a modest dress, but she was sent home with a note from the principle saying she was not to return to school wearing “that thing.” If ye be reproached for the name of Christ, happy are ye; for the spirit of glory and of God resteth upon you: on their part he is evil spoken of, but on your part he is glorified. –1Pe 4:14

Happiness comes from suffering for righteousness. Biblical suffering comes from obeying Jesus in the face of opposition. Are we too busy arguing over personal opinions of doctrine and being politically correct while the world laughs at us and goes to hell? Let’s be like Jesus and faithful Christians down through the ages, living in a manner so that those around us cannot deny that the power of God is in us. We have something that everyone needs. So, what are we waiting for? Let’s reunite, gather back together, deny ourselves, pick up our crosses and follow him!

Før jeg ble omvendt, hadde jeg aldri hørt betegnelsen «anabaptist», og tanken på at noen skulle dele sin tro på Jesus med andre, var fremmed for meg. Etter at jeg ble omvendt, husker jeg at jeg tenkte på alle vennene mine som ikke visste noe om det som nettopp hadde skjedd med meg. Én ting gikk stadig gjennom hodet mitt: «Jeg må fortelle dem det!» Når noe godt skjer med noen, forteller de det vanligvis til andre. Noen forteller det til én eller to, mens andre får lyst til å fortelle det til alle. Det var det jeg ønsket å gjøre, ikke for min egen skyld, men for deres.

Hver gang jeg traff en gammel venn, fortalte jeg dem hva som hadde skjedd med meg. Vanligvis sa de at de hadde hørt om det, og prøvde så å få meg til å roe meg ned og slappe av. Jeg skal være den første til å innrømme at jeg gjorde feil de første årene. Jeg merket at mange ikke satte pris på det jeg hadde å si, men det som forbløffet meg mest, var at de som hevdet å være kristne, så ut til å bli mest fornærmet.

En dag var jeg på besøk hos en eldre mann som sa at han hadde vært kristen det meste av livet. Under samtalen pekte han opp på en lyspære og sa: «Ser du den lyspæren? Den snakker ikke.» Jeg ble sjokkert. Han fortalte meg at ja, Jesus sier at vi er verdens lys, men at lys er stille. De snakker ikke. Jeg dro hjem for å studere saken i Bibelen på egen hånd. Var dette sant? Det tok ikke lang tid før jeg fant vers som: Og Jesus vandret omkring i hele Galilea, underviste i synagogene deres, forkynte evangeliet om riket og helbredet alle slags sykdommer og plager blant folket. –Matt 4:23. Også i Matteus sier Jesus at han fikk medfølelse, fordi menneskene som var sammen med ham, var slitne og spredt omkring. Litt lenger framme leser vi: Da sa han til disiplene sine: «Høsten er rik, men arbeiderne er få. Be derfor høstens herre om å sende arbeidere ut til høsten sin.» –Matt 9:37-38

Det virker for meg som om Jesus snakket med folk om riket overalt hvor han dro. Jeg har sett mennesker vitne om Gud på en stygg måte. Det betyr ikke at vi ikke skal vitne. Hvis du leser Apostlenes gjerninger, er det omtrent alt du ser – troende som deler evangeliets budskap med andre! I én beretning tok myndighetene disiplene til fange og sa at de kunne slippe fri hvis de holdt munn! Men disiplene sa at de ikke kunne det: For vi kan ikke la være å tale om det vi har sett og hørt. –Apg 4:20. Til slutt ble de for alltid brakt til taushet – ved døden.

Senere hørte jeg om disse menneskene som kalles anabaptister. Jeg begynte å lese om dem, og om hvordan heller ikke de ville tie. Jeg bestilte Martyrspeilet og ble slått av det jeg leste. Disse kjære menneskene levde som disiplene vi finner i Bibelen. De oppfylte det Jesus sa: Og dere skal bli hatet av alle for mitt navns skyld. Men den som holder ut til enden, skal bli frelst. –Matt 10:22. Og i Romerbrevet: Som det står skrevet: For din skyld blir vi drept dagen lang, vi blir regnet som slaktesauer. –Rom 8:36. Etter en tid fant jeg en menighet med en anabaptistisk visjon.

Så hvorfor skriver jeg dette? Kjære brødre og søstre, jeg tror ilden er i ferd med å slukne. Jeg hører stadig noen av våre anabaptister snakke om å leve et stille og fredelig liv. Jesus sier i lignelsen om såmannen: Den som ble sådd blant tornene, er den som hører ordet, men bekymringene i denne verden og rikdommens bedrag kveler ordet, og han blir ufruktbar. –Matt 13:22. Kan det være slik det står til med noen av oss? Vi lever i en vestlig kultur der penger synes å være lette å få tak i, og vi blir opptatt av vår egen rikdom og bekymringene i denne verden. La oss passe på at vi ikke blir lik verden for å unngå å bli forfulgt av verden.

En gruppe anabaptister flyktet fra forfølgelse og dro til et land der de ennå ikke ble forfulgt. De startet et møbelverksted for å forsørge seg, men klarte ikke å selge noen møbler fordi de var de fryktede anabaptistene. Snart ble situasjonen desperat fordi de trengte penger til mat. En dag kom en rik mann inn i verkstedet. Alle arbeiderne sluttet å jobbe. «Kanskje denne mannen kjøper noe, så vi kan få mat!» tenkte de. En eldre bror gikk bort til den mulige kunden og spurte om han kjente Jesus. Etter en kort samtale stormet mannen rasende ut av butikken. Snart spurte noen sultne arbeidere den gamle mannen hvorfor han måtte skremme bort deres eneste mulighet til å få solgt noe. Han forklarte at det var langt viktigere at denne mannen skulle kjenne Jesus enn at de skulle bekymre seg for å få solgt noe. Slik tenkte de tidlige anabaptistene – evangeliet kom først. De kunne ikke la være å tale om det de hadde sett og hørt, og også de ble drept dagen lang.

Jeg har lest mange beretninger om tidlige anabaptistiske kristne som ble arrestert for sin tro. Myndighetene bønnfalt dem om bare å holde munn! Men de nektet, slik disiplene gjorde. Også de valgte døden framfor et stille liv. En ung mann ble arrestert og etterlot seg sin kjære kone, som ventet deres første barn. Myndighetene ventet til barnet var født, og brakte så det nyfødte barnet til den nybakte faren i fengselet. De fortalte ham at han nå var far, og at han kunne dra hjem og være sammen med kona og sønnen. De sa at han også kunne fortsette å tro på samme måte, men han måtte tie og ikke tale imot synd i kirken. Den unge faren nektet, så de brente ham på bålet. Det var ikke et alternativ å tie.

Så hva mener Skriften med et stille og fredelig liv? Paulus skriver til Timoteus: Først av alt formaner jeg derfor til at det bæres fram bønner, påkallelser, forbønner og takk for alle mennesker, for konger og alle som har myndighet, så vi kan leve et stille og fredelig liv i all gudsfrykt og verdighet. –1 Tim 2:1-2. For konger og alle som har myndighet, så vi kan leve et stille og fredelig liv i all gudsfrykt og verdighet? Ja, apostelen Paulus sier dette, men hva mente han? Kan han ha ment at vi skal tie om evangeliet? Eller at vi aldri skal konfrontere en synder? Paulus ber oss ikke om å gjøre noe han selv aldri gjorde, eller noe Kristus selv aldri gjorde. Tvert imot viser Skriften oss noe helt annet.

Det virker som om de nytestamentlige kristne i Bibelen og i den tidlige kirken aktivt spredte evangeliet og var begeistret for Jesu Kristi kirke. De dro omkring og forkynte evangeliet: De holdt møter i fjellene, i skogene eller hvor som helst folk ville komme. Det var livet deres. Her sier Paulus at vi skal be om at myndighetene lar oss være i fred mens vi utfører våre vanlige daglige gjøremål, dersom vi adlyder Gud ved å gjøre ting myndighetene ikke liker. Som kristne bør vi spre sannheten i Guds Ord og arbeide aktivt for å fremme Guds rike. Vi bør be om at myndighetene lar oss leve i fred mens vi tjener fredsfyrsten.

Noen kristne prøver å være som verden i sitt forsøk på å vinne verden. De prøver å få folk til å leve et lykkelig liv, bli med i klubben vår, være fri i Kristus, dra på en spennende misjonsreise, leve livet fullt ut og bli alt de kan bli. Alt handler om å «elske Jesus», ikke om å adlyde ham.

Hva med oss? Er vi ivrige etter å fortelle folk om Jesus, selv om det vil koste oss noe? For mange av oss er det ganske lett å snakke om gårdsdrift, byggearbeid, hjortejakt og mye annet, men når det gjelder det som har med Gud å gjøre, har vi ikke stort å si. Er vi så redde for forfølgelse? Frykter vi at verden skal hate oss? Husk hva Jesus sa: Hvis verden hater dere, så vit at den har hatet meg før dere. Hvis dere var av verden, ville verden elsket sitt eget … –Joh 15:18-19. Og: Den som skammer seg over meg og mine ord i denne utro og syndige slekt, ham skal også Menneskesønnen skamme seg over når han kommer i sin Fars herlighet sammen med de hellige englene. –Mark 8:38

Det er lett å være kristen når man slår seg til ro og lever et stille og fredelig liv, aldri utfordrer en synder, aldri irettesetter en bror eller tråkker Satan på tærne, men hvem har sagt at det skulle være lett? Her på Haiti prøver vi som menighet å følge Jesus uansett hva det koster. Bare i går fortalte to medlemmer oss at de står i fare for å miste jobbene sine på grunn av evangeliet. En annen søster i menigheten fortalte at skolen barna hennes går på, krever uniformer, og at jentene må ha på seg bukser. Hun sendte datteren sin på skolen i en anstendig kjole, men hun ble sendt hjem med en beskjed fra rektoren om at hun ikke måtte komme tilbake til skolen iført «den greia der». Hvis dere blir hånet for Kristi navns skyld, er dere salige, for herlighetens og Guds Ånd hviler over dere. Fra deres side blir han spottet, men fra deres side blir han æret. –1 Pet 4:14

Gleden kommer av å lide for rettferdighetens skyld. Bibelsk lidelse kommer av å adlyde Jesus når man møter motstand. Er vi for opptatt med å krangle om personlige meninger om læren og være politisk korrekte mens verden ler av oss og går fortapt? La oss være som Jesus og trofaste kristne gjennom tidene, og leve slik at menneskene omkring oss ikke kan benekte at Guds kraft er i oss. Vi har noe alle trenger. Så hva venter vi på? La oss forenes igjen, komme sammen på nytt, fornekte oss selv, ta opp korsene våre og følge ham!

Mile after mile sped by as Carol drove the old Chevy along the busy interstate highway toward home. Between intervals of silence and conversation, Carol and her two sisters, Elaine and Gloria, lifted their voices in song, giving thanks and praise to their Creator. How thankful they were for the opportunity to spend the evening with their friends at Pine Creek Church and to receive another inspiring message from God’s Word.

Suddenly their smooth travel was interrupted by signs of trouble. “Now what can be wrong with this car?” Carol worried out loud as she guided the stalled car to the side of the road. “Oh, no, girls, we’re out of gas! I was in such a hurry this evening that I forgot to check the gauge. I thought the tank was almost full when we left home, and… Oh no!” wailed Carol again. “Dad put the cell phone on the counter for me to take along, and I forgot that also!”

“Whatever are we going to do now?” exclaimed Elaine. “Here we are, stranded in the dark, no gas, no phone, and seven more miles to our exit! And another thing, people just don’t stop very quickly these days and offer help. They know that most everyone carries a phone. This seems almost impossible to me!” she mournfully uttered from the back seat.

As the girls lapsed into silence, the old Chevy seemed to shake in protest as a long row of trucks whizzed by. “You know,” said Gloria, “I was just remembering Brother Lester’s message this evening. How can we forget so quickly! Maybe God has allowed this to happen to us so our faith might be increased as we place our trust in Him. Let’s take this to the Lord in prayer. Let’s look for a miracle from God’s hand.”

Together the girls bowed their heads and pled for the Lord’s protection and help.

“You know, I feel better already,” smiled Elaine. “I was so worried and fearful, but since we prayed and committed everything to God, I have confidence that He will watch over us. I’m so glad we have a God who hears all of our cries. What would we do without His comforting Holy Spirit? Let’s sing again.”

“Joys are flowing like a river,
Since the Comforter has come;
He abides with us forever,
Makes the trusting heart His home.
Blessed quietness, holy quietness,
Blest assurance in my soul!
On the stormy sea Jesus speaks to me,
And the billows cease to roll!”

-Manie P. Ferguson, 19th century

As the girls sang song after song, their hearts were deeply stirred. How quiet and peaceful they felt, even though they were stranded on a dark highway thirteen miles from home. Car after car, and truck after truck sped by without stopping. Then they noticed a pickup truck, with two dirt bikes on the back, slowing down. It pulled off the road several hundred feet ahead of them, and slowly began to back up. The girls’ voices were stilled in silence as they desperately cried out to God from the bottom of their hearts. When the truck came to a halt, two husky, long-haired men jumped out. Carol rolled her window down as a man wearing a red-checked flannel jacket approached.

“What’s the trouble here, girls?” he asked, glancing over the car.

“We’re out of gas,” Carol quickly replied.

“Well, I’d say we’re pretty lucky. We have a can of gas with us. How far do you need to go yet?”

“About thirteen miles.”

“Good. We’ll just pour some of our gas into your tank and you can be on your way again. No payment necessary.”

“O thank you so much,” responded Carol. “We were praying that God would send us help, and He did more than we could ever have thought! Thanks so much.”

“Yes, yes”, replied the man gruffly, “You’re pretty lucky we came along. We’re just glad to help you out.”

Several minutes later, the girls were on their way again. “You know,” said Carol, “when I saw that truck pull over, I was scared and glad at the same time. I began to scold myself again for not having that cell phone with me. But then I asked God to help me completely trust in Him and not be afraid. After all, isn’t He much more dependable than any cell phone? This has been such a faith booster for me. How different this may have turned out, if we had depended solely on our cell phones or “good luck” as those men called it. It must grieve our Father’s heart tremendously when we do not place our trust in Him.”

“It’s just as Brother Lester preached this evening”, added Gloria. “Remember some of those verses? I waited patiently for the LORD; and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry … And he hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God… Blessed is that man that maketh the LORD his trust, and respecteth not the proud, nor such as turn aside to lies. –Psa 40:1-4. This makes me so happy I just want to keep singing and thanking the Lord!”

Again, the girls raised their voices in song:

“His eye is always watching,
His ear is keen to hear;
His love is all-sufficient
To calm the gravest fear.
Then trust Him in shine and shade;
Trust Him, be not afraid:
He’s walking close beside thee;
His hand will safely guide thee;
His wings securely hide thee;
Then trust! Be not afraid.”

-Charles H. Gabriel, 1856-1932
